prompt: A company has an existing domain named corp.contoso.com. An administrator has installed the AD DS server role on a new Windows Server 2025 member server and must promote it to an additional writable domain controller for that domain by using PowerShell. Which cmdlet should the administrator run?

options.text: Install-ADDSForest
Install-ADDSDomain
Install-ADDSDomainController
Add-ADDSReadOnlyDomainControllerAccount

explanation: Install-ADDSDomainController adds a domain controller, writable or read-only, to an existing domain. Install-ADDSForest creates a new forest and Install-ADDSDomain creates a new child or tree domain. Add-ADDSReadOnlyDomainControllerAccount only pre-creates (stages) an RODC account and doesn't promote a writable DC.

prompt: A branch office connects to the main datacenter over a slow, heavily used WAN link. The administrator must deploy a new domain controller in the branch while minimizing the amount of directory data that crosses the WAN during promotion. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Clone an existing virtualized domain controller by using a DCCloneConfig.xml file and Hyper-V export
Create media with ntdsutil ifm on an existing DC and promote the server by using Install from Media
Increase the replication interval on the site link that connects the branch to the datacenter
Enable universal group membership caching for the branch site before promoting the server

explanation: Install from Media (IFM) lets the new DC take its initial copy of the directory, and optionally SYSVOL, from media created with ntdsutil ifm, so only changes made since the media was created replicate over the WAN. Cloning requires copying the exported source DC virtual machine to the branch host, which doesn't reduce the data moved across the WAN. The site link interval affects ongoing replication rather than the initial sync, and universal group membership caching only reduces global catalog lookups at logon.

prompt: An administrator plans to deploy several new domain controllers by cloning an existing virtualized Windows Server domain controller on Hyper-V. Before exporting the source DC, the administrator must authorize it to be cloned. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add the source DC's computer account to the Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers group
Add the source DC's computer account to the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group
Add the source DC's computer account to the Windows Authorization Access Group
Add the source DC's computer account to the Cloneable Domain Controllers group

explanation: A source domain controller must be a member of the Cloneable Domain Controllers group before it can be cloned, and the administrator also creates a DCCloneConfig.xml file, for example with New-ADDCCloneConfigFile. Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers holds RODCs, the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group controls which passwords RODCs can cache, and the Windows Authorization Access Group grants read access to token group information; none of them authorizes cloning.

prompt: An administrator is deploying a domain controller on an Azure virtual machine. Where should the AD DS database, log files and SYSVOL be placed?

options.text: On a separate managed data disk with host caching set to None
On the operating system disk with host caching set to Read/Write
On the temporary disk so that they use the local SSD of the host
On a separate managed data disk with host caching set to Read-only

explanation: Microsoft recommends placing NTDS.dit, its logs and SYSVOL on a data disk whose host cache preference is None, because host caching can undermine the database's write-through behavior. The OS disk uses Read/Write caching by default, which isn't suitable for AD DS data, and Read-only caching isn't the recommended setting either. The temporary disk isn't persistent and its contents can be lost during maintenance or redeployment.

prompt: An administrator deployed a Windows Server VM in Azure to act as a domain controller. To keep its address from changing, the administrator typed a static IPv4 address into the guest operating system's network adapter settings, and the VM then lost network connectivity. What is the recommended way to give the DC a fixed address?

options.text: Assign a Standard SKU public IP address to the VM and configure it as the DNS server on the VNet
Create a DHCP reservation on an on-premises DHCP server for the VM's MAC address
Set the Azure NIC's private IP allocation to Static and keep the guest adapter on DHCP
Use netsh in the guest to set a static IP address outside the subnet's address range

explanation: Azure assigns a VM's private IP address from the platform, so a fixed address is configured by setting the Azure network interface's allocation to Static while the guest adapter stays on DHCP; setting a static IP inside the guest can cut the VM off the network. A public IP address isn't used for traffic inside the VNet and exposes the DC unnecessarily. On-premises DHCP reservations don't apply to Azure VNets, and an address outside the subnet can't be routed by Azure.

prompt: A company extends its on-premises AD DS forest to Azure by deploying two domain controllers in an Azure virtual network. New member VMs in the VNet fail to join the domain because they can't locate a domain controller. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Keep Azure-provided DNS on the VNet and create a CNAME record for the domain name
Create an Azure Private DNS zone for the AD domain name with autoregistration enabled
Create an Azure public DNS zone for the AD domain and add A records for the DCs
Set the VNet's custom DNS servers to the domain controllers' private IP addresses

explanation: Clients locate DCs through the SRV records in the AD-integrated DNS zones hosted on the DCs, so the VNet's DNS servers should be the DCs' private IP addresses. Azure-provided DNS can't resolve those SRV records, and a CNAME doesn't supply them. A Private DNS zone with autoregistration only registers VM A records and doesn't host the dynamically registered DC records, and a public DNS zone exposes internal names while still lacking the SRV records.

prompt: An administrator wants a branch office technician, who isn't a member of Domain Admins, to finish installing a read-only domain controller at the branch. The administrator wants to keep control of the RODC's name, site and password replication policy. What should the administrator do first?

options.text: Stage the RODC account and name the technician as its delegated administrator
Add the technician to the domain's Server Operators group for the duration of the installation
Add the technician to the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group so the technician's credentials are cached
Give the technician Install from Media files and have the technician run Install-ADDSForest

explanation: Staging an RODC creates its computer account in advance with the chosen name, site and replication policy, and a delegated user or group can then attach the server to that account without Domain Admins rights. Server Operators doesn't grant the right to promote a DC and is a privileged group that should stay empty. The Allowed RODC Password Replication Group only affects credential caching, and Install-ADDSForest creates a new forest rather than an RODC.

prompt: A local technician must install drivers and updates on a branch office RODC. The technician needs administrative rights on that RODC only, with no rights on other domain controllers or in the domain. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Add the technician to the domain's built-in Administrators group
Add the technician to the Backup Operators group
Configure the technician as the delegated administrator of the RODC by using administrator role separation
Add the technician to the Allow list of the RODC's Password Replication Policy

explanation: Administrator role separation delegates local administrative permissions on one RODC, set when staging the account or later with dsmgmt local roles, without granting rights in the domain. The built-in Administrators group in a domain applies to every domain controller, and Backup Operators can sign in to and back up any DC. Allowing the technician's password to be cached grants no administrative rights.

prompt: A company has RODCs in several branch offices. The administrator must ensure that only the RODC in the Denver branch can cache the passwords of members of the Denver-Users group. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add Denver-Users to the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group
Add Denver-Users to the Allow list in the Password Replication Policy of the Denver RODC
Add Denver-Users to the Denied RODC Password Replication Group
Add Denver-Users to the Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers group

explanation: Each RODC has its own Password Replication Policy, so adding the group to the Denver RODC's Allow list permits caching on that RODC only. The Allowed RODC Password Replication Group is in the Allow list of every RODC in the domain by default, so it would allow caching on all branch RODCs. The Denied RODC Password Replication Group blocks caching, and Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers is meant for RODC computer accounts.

prompt: A user belongs to a group that is on the Allow list of a branch RODC's Password Replication Policy. The user is also a member of Account Operators. After several sign-ins at the branch, the user's password still hasn't been cached on the RODC. What is the reason?

options.text: Passwords are cached only after an administrator runs repadmin /prp add on the RODC for each account
An RODC caches only computer account passwords until it is restarted
The user must sign in at least ten times before the password is cached
Account Operators is on every RODC's Deny list by default, and Deny overrides Allow

explanation: By default each RODC's Password Replication Policy denies Account Operators, Administrators, Backup Operators, Server Operators and the Denied RODC Password Replication Group, and Deny always wins over Allow. For allowed accounts, caching happens automatically after a successful authentication, so no repadmin command or minimum number of sign-ins is needed. RODCs cache user as well as computer passwords when the policy allows it.

prompt: A new RODC is being deployed to a remote site whose WAN link often fails. Users at the site must be able to sign in through the RODC even if the WAN fails before they've signed in there for the first time. Their group is already on the RODC's Allow list. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Prepopulate the passwords of the users' accounts on the RODC
Enable universal group membership caching for the remote site
Configure the RODC as a global catalog server
Add the users to the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group

explanation: Prepopulating passwords, from the RODC's Password Replication Policy tab or with repadmin /rodcpwdrepl, caches allowed accounts' credentials before the users first sign in. Universal group membership caching and global catalog placement help with group lookups, not with credentials that haven't been cached. The group is already allowed, so adding it to another allow group caches nothing until users authenticate.

prompt: An RODC at a branch office has been stolen. The administrator must make sure attackers can't use any credentials that were cached on it. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Run ntdsutil metadata cleanup and then restart all writable domain controllers
Add all branch users to the Protected Users group
Delete the RODC's computer account and reset the passwords of the accounts cached on it
Remove the branch user group from the Allow list of the stolen RODC's Password Replication Policy

explanation: When an RODC account is deleted in Active Directory Users and Computers, the wizard can reset the passwords of all user and computer accounts that were cached on it and export the list, which makes the stolen credentials useless. Metadata cleanup removes server metadata but doesn't change any passwords. Changes to Protected Users or to the Password Replication Policy affect only future caching, not credentials already on the stolen device.

prompt: The domain controller that holds the RID master role has suffered a permanent hardware failure and won't be repaired. The administrator must move the role to DC2. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Run ntdsutil, connect to DC2 and use the transfer RID master command
Run Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity DC2 -OperationMasterRole RIDMaster -Force
Run netdom query fsmo on DC2
Restore the failed DC's system state backup onto DC2 in Directory Services Restore Mode

explanation: When the current role holder is permanently offline, the role must be seized; Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole with -Force seizes the role if a transfer can't be completed, and the failed DC must never return to the network. A transfer requires the current holder to be online. netdom query fsmo only reports role holders, and restoring another DC's system state onto DC2 isn't a supported way to move a role.

prompt: Before decommissioning an old server, an administrator needs to identify which domain controllers currently hold each of the five operations master roles. Which command lists them?

options.text: repadmin /showrepl
dcdiag /test:dns
nltest /dsgetdc:corp.contoso.com
netdom query fsmo

explanation: netdom query fsmo lists the holders of the schema master, domain naming master, RID master, PDC emulator and infrastructure master roles. repadmin /showrepl shows replication status, dcdiag /test:dns tests DNS health and nltest /dsgetdc locates a DC for a domain; none of them lists all role holders.

prompt: An application installer must extend the Active Directory schema, but the update fails because the required operations master can't be contacted. Which role holder must be online and reachable?

options.text: PDC emulator
Infrastructure master
Schema master
Domain naming master

explanation: Only the schema master can write changes to the schema, so it must be available for schema extensions. The PDC emulator handles password change forwarding and time, the infrastructure master updates cross-domain references, and the domain naming master controls adding and removing domains and application partitions.

prompt: On a newly promoted domain controller, administrators can't create users or groups, and the Directory Service event log reports that the DC couldn't obtain a new pool of relative identifiers. Which role holder is most likely unavailable?

options.text: RID master
PDC emulator
Infrastructure master
Schema master

explanation: Each DC receives blocks of relative identifiers from the RID master and needs them to build SIDs for new security principals, so it can't create those objects without a RID pool. The PDC emulator, infrastructure master and schema master don't allocate RID pools.

prompt: An administrator plans to create a new AD DS forest by promoting a Windows Server 2025 server. A legacy application vendor asks for the new forest to use the Windows Server 2012 R2 forest functional level. What is the outcome?

options.text: The forest can be created at the Windows Server 2012 R2 level and raised later
The forest can be created at the Windows Server 2012 R2 level only if the 32k database page size feature stays disabled
The forest must use the Windows Server 2025 functional level, the only level a Windows Server 2025 DC supports
The forest can't be created at that level, because new forests require a functional level of Windows Server 2016 or later

explanation: New Active Directory forests require a functional level of Windows Server 2016 or later, so the Windows Server 2012 R2 level isn't available when creating the forest. Windows Server 2025 DCs also run in domains and forests at Windows Server 2016 or higher levels, so the 2025 level isn't mandatory. The optional 32k database page size feature doesn't change the minimum level for a new forest.

prompt: Two companies, each with its own single-domain AD DS forest, have merged. Users in every domain of each forest must be able to access resources in every domain of the other forest, including child domains that may be added later. Which trust should the administrator create?

options.text: A two-way external trust between the forest root domains
A two-way forest trust between the forest root domains
A shortcut trust between the forest root domains
A realm trust between the forest root domains

explanation: A forest trust is transitive across all domains in both forests, so child domains added later are covered automatically. An external trust is non-transitive and covers only the two domains it connects. Shortcut trusts link domains within one forest, and realm trusts connect to non-Windows Kerberos v5 realms.

prompt: An administrator tries to create a forest trust between contoso.com and fabrikam.com, but the New Trust Wizard reports that it can't find the other domain. Each forest uses its own DNS servers. What should the administrator configure first?

options.text: Conditional forwarders or stub zones for each other's domain names
A shortcut trust between the two forest root domains, created from either side
Name suffix routing on the forest trust
Selective authentication on the forest trust

explanation: Creating a forest trust requires each forest to resolve the other's domain name and DC records, which is normally done with conditional forwarders or stub zones. Shortcut trusts are only for domains in the same forest. Name suffix routing and selective authentication are properties of an existing trust and don't fix name resolution.

prompt: Contoso has a two-way forest trust with Fabrikam. Only members of the Fabrikam group Finance-Auditors may authenticate to two specific Contoso file servers, and other Fabrikam users must not be able to authenticate to any Contoso computer. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Enable SID filtering on the trust and add Finance-Auditors to a domain local group
Replace the forest trust with an external trust between the root domains
Enable selective authentication and grant Finance-Auditors Allowed to Authenticate on the two servers
Disable name suffix routing for fabrikam.com and grant Finance-Auditors NTFS permissions on the servers

explanation: With selective authentication, users from the trusted forest can authenticate only to computers where they've been granted the Allowed to Authenticate permission. SID filtering strips foreign SIDs such as SID history but doesn't limit which computers users reach. An external trust removes transitivity without restricting authentication, and disabling name suffix routing would break authentication for every Fabrikam user, including the auditors.

prompt: A forest contains two trees, contoso.com and fabrikam.com. Users in sales.eu.contoso.com often access servers in hr.na.fabrikam.com, and authentication is slow because Kerberos referrals traverse the whole trust path. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A forest trust between contoso.com and fabrikam.com
An external trust between contoso.com and fabrikam.com
A realm trust between sales.eu.contoso.com and hr.na.fabrikam.com
A shortcut trust between sales.eu.contoso.com and hr.na.fabrikam.com

explanation: A shortcut trust between two domains in the same forest shortens the referral path between them. A forest trust connects separate forests, not trees within one forest, and an external trust between the tree roots wouldn't shorten the path for the child domains. Realm trusts are only for non-Windows Kerberos realms.

prompt: A research department runs a Linux-based MIT Kerberos v5 realm. Administrators want AD DS users to access services in that realm by using Kerberos. Which type of trust should be created?

options.text: External trust
Realm trust
Forest trust
Shortcut trust

explanation: A realm trust connects an AD DS domain with a non-Windows Kerberos v5 realm and can be transitive or non-transitive. External, forest and shortcut trusts work only between Windows domains or forests.

prompt: Users were migrated with SID history from a domain in another forest. They still need to reach resources in the old domain across an external trust, but access granted to their old SIDs fails. Which trust feature causes this?

options.text: SID filtering, which is enabled by default on external trusts
Selective authentication, which is enabled by default on external trusts
Name suffix routing, which blocks UPN suffixes from the other forest
Kerberos AES support, which is required by default on external trusts

explanation: SID filtering removes SIDs that don't belong to the trusted domain from authentication data, which strips SID history entries; it's enabled by default on external trusts and can be relaxed with netdom trust /quarantine:no when it's safe to do so. Selective authentication isn't on by default and controls which computers users can authenticate to. Name suffix routing applies to forest trusts, and AES encryption support doesn't remove SIDs from tokens.

prompt: Fabrikam added a new UPN suffix, fabrikam-research.com, to its forest. Users who use this suffix to sign in to Contoso resources across an existing forest trust fail to authenticate, while users with the original suffix succeed. What should the Contoso administrator do?

options.text: Replace the forest trust with an external trust
Enable selective authentication on the trust
Enable routing for the new suffix on the Name Suffix Routing tab of the trust's properties
Add fabrikam-research.com as an alternative UPN suffix in the Contoso forest

explanation: Name suffixes added to a trusted forest after the trust exists may appear but not be enabled for routing, so authentication requests that use them aren't sent to the trusted forest until routing is enabled. External trusts don't support name suffix routing. Selective authentication restricts access instead of fixing routing, and adding the same suffix in Contoso would create a conflict with the suffix that Fabrikam owns.

prompt: Users in the Contoso forest need access to resources in the Fabrikam forest. Fabrikam users must not gain access to Contoso resources. How should the one-way forest trust be configured?

options.text: Contoso trusts Fabrikam, so the trust is outgoing from Contoso
Fabrikam is the trusted forest and Contoso is the trusting forest
Each forest trusts the other, with selective authentication enabled in Contoso
Fabrikam trusts Contoso, so the trust is outgoing from Fabrikam and incoming to Contoso

explanation: The forest that holds the resources trusts the forest whose users need access, so Fabrikam (resources) trusts Contoso (accounts), creating an outgoing trust in Fabrikam and an incoming trust in Contoso. The first two options describe the reverse direction, which would let Fabrikam users reach Contoso resources. A two-way trust grants access in both directions, which the requirement forbids.

prompt: A company opened a branch office that uses the subnet 10.20.0.0/24 and created an AD DS site named Branch with its own domain controller. Clients in the branch still authenticate against domain controllers at the head office. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The branch domain controller isn't a global catalog server
No subnet object for 10.20.0.0/24 is associated with the Branch site
The site link between the sites has too low a cost
Universal group membership caching isn't enabled for the Branch site

explanation: Clients find their site by matching their IP address to subnet objects, so without a subnet object linked to the Branch site the DC Locator can't point them to the branch DC. Global catalog placement and universal group membership caching affect group lookups, not which site a client belongs to. Site link cost influences replication paths and fallback DC choice, not client site assignment.

prompt: The Paris site has two site links to the London site, one over dedicated fiber and one over a backup VPN. Replication should use the fiber link and fall back to the VPN only when the fiber link is unavailable. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Set a shorter replication interval on the VPN site link
Add both site links to a site link bridge
Assign a lower cost to the fiber site link than to the VPN site link
Clear the replication schedule on the fiber site link

explanation: The KCC chooses the lowest-cost path, so a lower cost on the fiber link makes it preferred while the VPN link remains available for failover. The replication interval sets how often replication happens, not which link is used. A site link bridge models transitivity between links, and removing the fiber link's schedule would stop replication on the preferred path.

prompt: Two AD DS sites are connected by a high-capacity, low-latency link. The business wants directory changes to replicate between the sites within seconds, as they do inside a site, rather than on a schedule. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Enable change notification on the site link that connects the two sites
Set the replication interval on the site link to 15 minutes
Set the cost of the site link to 1
Create a site link bridge that contains the site link

explanation: Enabling change notification on a site link, through its options attribute, makes intersite replication notification-based like replication within a site. Fifteen minutes is the shortest scheduled interval a site link supports, which is still far longer than seconds. Cost only affects path selection, and a site link bridge affects transitive routing rather than replication speed.

prompt: A small branch site has one domain controller that isn't a global catalog. The forest has several domains and uses universal groups. When the WAN link fails, branch users can't sign in. The administrator must fix this without making the branch DC a global catalog. What should be done?

options.text: Make the branch DC the preferred bridgehead server for the site
Add the branch users to the Allowed RODC Password Replication Group
Lower the cost of the site link to the head office
Enable universal group membership caching for the branch site

explanation: Universal group membership caching lets the site's DC cache each user's universal group memberships after the first sign-in, so later sign-ins don't need a global catalog across the WAN. A preferred bridgehead server only controls intersite replication endpoints. The Allowed RODC Password Replication Group applies to RODCs, and site link cost doesn't help when the WAN is down.

prompt: The firewall between two sites allows AD DS replication traffic only between domain controllers DC-HQ1 and DC-BR1. The administrator must make intersite replication use only these servers. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Make DC-HQ1 and DC-BR1 global catalog servers so that they host all partitions
Make DC-HQ1 and DC-BR1 the preferred bridgehead servers in their sites
Create manual connection objects between every DC in both sites
Disable the KCC in both sites and enable change notification

explanation: Preferred bridgehead servers restrict the intersite topology generator to those DCs when it creates intersite connections, so replication between sites flows only through them. Global catalog status doesn't affect which DCs replicate between sites. Manual connections between every DC would break the firewall rules, and disabling the KCC with change notification doesn't restrict which servers replicate.

prompt: A company's WAN isn't fully routed: Tokyo can reach Singapore and Singapore can reach Sydney, but Tokyo can't reach Sydney. The KCC keeps creating replication connections between Tokyo and Sydney DCs, and they fail. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Increase the cost of the Tokyo-Singapore site link so that the KCC prefers other paths
Enable universal group membership caching in the Tokyo site
Disable Bridge all site links and create site link bridges only where routing exists
Make every domain controller a global catalog server so that all partitions are available locally

explanation: By default all site links are bridged, which tells the KCC that any site can reach any other; in a network that isn't fully routed, you disable that setting and create explicit site link bridges. Changing cost doesn't remove the false transitivity. Universal group membership caching and global catalog placement don't affect the replication topology.

prompt: An administrator changed a critical object in Active Directory and must push the change immediately from the current DC to all domain controllers in every site, without waiting for the schedule. Which command should be used?

options.text: repadmin /syncall /AdeP
repadmin /replsummary
dcdiag /test:replications
gpupdate /force

explanation: repadmin /syncall with /A (all partitions), /d (distinguished names), /e (enterprise, across sites) and /P (push) forces replication from the DC to all its partners. repadmin /replsummary and dcdiag /test:replications only report replication health, and gpupdate /force refreshes Group Policy on a computer.

prompt: A user changes their password on a branch domain controller and immediately signs in at another site whose DC hasn't yet received the change. The sign-in with the new password succeeds. Which mechanism makes this possible?

options.text: Urgent replication of all password changes to every DC
Universal group membership caching on the second DC storing the user's new credentials
The RID master validating the user's credentials
Other DCs check with the PDC emulator, which receives password changes first

explanation: Password changes are replicated preferentially to the PDC emulator, and a DC that can't validate a password forwards the request to the PDC emulator, which has the newest password. Password changes aren't urgently replicated to every DC, and neither universal group membership caching nor the RID master takes part in password validation.

prompt: An administrator tries to promote a Windows Server 2025 server as a domain controller in a domain that was upgraded over many years from Windows Server 2003. Promotion fails with a message about the SYSVOL replication technology. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Raise the forest functional level to Windows Server 2025 before promotion
Migrate SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFS Replication by using dfsrmig
Promote the server with Install from Media so SYSVOL isn't replicated
Enable the AD Recycle Bin and retry the promotion

explanation: Domain controllers running Windows Server 2019 and later can't join a domain that still replicates SYSVOL with FRS, so SYSVOL must first be migrated to DFS Replication with dfsrmig. The functional level can't be raised above the level of the existing DCs and isn't the cause. Install from Media doesn't remove the SYSVOL replication requirement, and the AD Recycle Bin is unrelated.

prompt: Users in three domains of the same forest need Modify permission on a shared folder on a file server in the corp.contoso.com domain. Following Microsoft's recommended group nesting strategy, how should access be granted?

options.text: Add users from all three domains directly to a global group in corp.contoso.com and assign it permissions
Add users from all three domains to a domain local group and assign permissions to each user
Nest global groups from each domain in a domain local group in corp.contoso.com and grant permissions to it
Add users to domain local groups in their own domains and nest those groups in a global group in corp.contoso.com

explanation: The AGDLP strategy puts accounts in global groups, nests the global groups in a domain local group in the resource domain and assigns permissions to that domain local group. A global group can contain members only from its own domain, so it can't hold users from the other domains. Assigning permissions per user defeats group management, and domain local groups can't be members of global groups.

prompt: An administrator needs a group that can contain global groups from every domain in the forest and can be granted permissions on resources in any domain of the forest. Which group scope should be used?

options.text: Universal
Global
Domain local
Built-in local

explanation: Universal groups can contain accounts and global groups from any domain in the forest and can be granted permissions in any domain; their membership is stored in the global catalog. Global groups contain members only from their own domain, domain local groups can be granted permissions only in their own domain, and built-in local groups are limited to their domain or computer.

prompt: An administrator tries to change a global security group named Sales-G directly to domain local scope, but the option isn't available. Sales-G isn't a member of any other global group. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Change the group type to distribution, and then change the scope to domain local
Delete the group and create a domain local group that reuses its SID
Raise the domain functional level so that the conversion becomes available
Convert Sales-G to universal scope first, and then convert it from universal to domain local

explanation: A global group can't be converted straight to domain local; it can become universal when it isn't a member of another global group, and a universal group can then be converted to domain local. Changing the group type doesn't alter the scope conversion rules. A new group always receives a new SID, and the functional level doesn't control scope conversion.

prompt: An administrator receives a CSV file listing 400 new employees with columns for name, sAMAccountName, department and OU path, and must create their AD DS accounts with as little effort as possible. What should be used?

options.text: The dsadd user command, run once for each row
Import-Csv piped to a loop that runs New-ADUser with values from each row
Active Directory Administrative Center with a copied user template
ldifde -i with the CSV file as the input file

explanation: Import-Csv turns each row into an object whose properties can be passed to New-ADUser, so one script creates all the accounts. dsadd and Active Directory Administrative Center require one operation per user. ldifde imports LDIF-formatted files, not CSV.

prompt: A contractor's AD DS account must stop working automatically at the end of 30 June, without an administrator acting on that day. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: The account expiration date on the contractor's user account
A fine-grained password policy whose maximum password age ends on 30 June
Logon hours on the account that deny sign-in after 30 June
The msDS-UserPasswordExpiryTimeComputed attribute set to 30 June

explanation: The account expiration setting, on the Account tab or with Set-ADAccountExpiration, blocks sign-in automatically after the chosen date. A maximum password age forces a password change rather than ending access, and logon hours repeat weekly and can't express a calendar date. msDS-UserPasswordExpiryTimeComputed is a constructed, read-only attribute that can't be set.

prompt: Contoso has a forest trust with Fabrikam. A Contoso administrator wants to grant a Fabrikam global group access to a Contoso file share by adding it to a Contoso group. Which Contoso group can contain the Fabrikam group?

options.text: A global security group
A universal security group
A domain local security group
A global distribution group

explanation: Domain local groups can contain users and groups from trusted external domains and forests, which appear as foreign security principals. Global groups contain members only from their own domain, and universal groups can contain members from any domain in their own forest but not from another forest. Distribution groups can't be used to assign permissions.

prompt: The AD DS domain is named corp.local, but users should sign in with names such as user@contoso.com that match their email addresses. What should the administrator do first?

options.text: Rename the domain to contoso.com by using the rendom domain rename tool
Create a new tree domain named contoso.com in the forest
Create a contoso.com DNS zone on the domain controllers
Add contoso.com as a UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts

explanation: Adding an alternative UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts, or with Set-ADForest -UPNSuffixes, lets administrators assign user@contoso.com as each user's UPN. Renaming a domain or adding a tree is disruptive and unnecessary. A DNS zone doesn't make a UPN suffix available to accounts.

prompt: During a merger, user accounts must move from the Fabrikam forest to the Contoso forest. The users must keep access to Fabrikam resources that are still secured with their original SIDs until those resources are re-permissioned. Which tool should be used?

options.text: Active Directory Migration Tool (ADMT) with SID history migration
ldifde to export the users from Fabrikam and import them into Contoso
csvde to export and import the user accounts
New-ADUser with the -Instance parameter based on each Fabrikam user

explanation: ADMT migrates accounts between forests and can populate the sIDHistory attribute so users keep access to resources secured with their original SIDs. ldifde, csvde and New-ADUser create new accounts with new SIDs and can't write SID history, so resource access would break.

prompt: A forest contains five domains. A help desk technician must find a user account by name without knowing which domain it's in. What should the technician query?

options.text: The PDC emulator of the forest root domain on port 389
A global catalog server on port 3268
The domain naming master on port 636
Any RODC in the forest root domain on port 389

explanation: The global catalog holds a partial replica of every object in the forest and answers forest-wide searches on port 3268, or 3269 with TLS. Queries to a DC on port 389 or 636 search only that DC's domain, and neither the PDC emulator nor the domain naming master holds forest-wide data in its domain partition.

prompt: An administrator runs New-ADServiceAccount to create the first group managed service account in a new forest and receives an error stating that the key doesn't exist. What must the administrator do?

options.text: Raise the domain functional level to Windows Server 2025
Install the Active Directory module for PowerShell on the server that will use the account
Create a Key Distribution Services root key by running Add-KdsRootKey
Add the server that will use the account to the Cloneable Domain Controllers group

explanation: gMSA passwords are derived from a Key Distribution Services root key, which is created once per forest with Add-KdsRootKey; DCs wait up to 10 hours before using a new key unless an earlier effective time is set in a lab. gMSAs don't require the Windows Server 2025 functional level. The AD module is already present because the cmdlet ran, and the Cloneable Domain Controllers group is used for DC cloning.

prompt: An application pool runs on six IIS servers in a load-balanced farm. The service identity must be identical on every server, and its password must change automatically. Which type of account should be used?

options.text: A standalone managed service account (sMSA)
A virtual account
A domain user account with Password never expires set
A group managed service account (gMSA)

explanation: A gMSA can be used by many computers at once and has its password managed automatically by AD DS, which suits a server farm. An sMSA can be used on only one computer, and a virtual account is local to one computer. A regular user account with a non-expiring password requires manual password management.

prompt: A gMSA named svc-web works on servers WEB1 and WEB2. After a new server, WEB3, joined the farm, Test-ADServiceAccount svc-web returns False on WEB3. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Run Install-ADServiceAccount svc-web again on WEB1 and then restart the application pools on WEB3
Add WEB3 to the gMSA's PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword with Set-ADServiceAccount
Reset the gMSA's password by using Set-ADAccountPassword
Create a new KDS root key by using Add-KdsRootKey

explanation: Only principals listed in PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword can retrieve a gMSA's password, so WEB3 must be added; if a group is used, WEB3 must restart or refresh its tickets to pick up the membership. Reinstalling the account on WEB1 doesn't affect WEB3. gMSA passwords are managed by AD DS rather than reset manually, and the existing KDS root key already works for WEB1 and WEB2.

prompt: In a domain with Windows Server 2025 domain controllers, an administrator has started migrating a legacy service account to a delegated managed service account (dMSA) and confirmed the service works. The original account must now be disabled so that all services use the dMSA. Which cmdlet should the administrator run?

options.text: Complete-ADServiceAccountMigration
Undo-ADServiceAccountMigration
Reset-ADServiceAccountMigration
Remove-ADServiceAccount

explanation: Complete-ADServiceAccountMigration finalizes the migration and disables the superseded service account. Undo-ADServiceAccountMigration reverses the migration steps, and Reset-ADServiceAccountMigration returns the account to an unlinked state. Remove-ADServiceAccount deletes a managed service account, and Microsoft warns against deleting the original account because it may be needed to revert.

prompt: A custom Windows service runs on one member server. It needs local resources and network access as the computer account only. The administrator wants no password management and no new AD DS objects. Which identity should the service use?

options.text: A group managed service account
A domain user account in the Domain Users group
A virtual account such as NT SERVICE\ServiceName
A standalone managed service account

explanation: Virtual accounts are created automatically by the service control manager, need no password management or AD object and access the network with the computer's credentials. gMSAs and sMSAs both require AD DS objects, and a domain user account requires manual password management.

prompt: A large multi-domain forest uses universal groups to grant access to forest-wide applications. User membership changes are frequent, and administrators want to minimize the global catalog replication those changes cause. What should they do?

options.text: Convert the universal groups to domain local groups in each domain
Add users directly to the universal groups and enable universal group membership caching
Replace the universal groups with universal distribution groups
Nest global groups from each domain in the universal groups instead of adding users

explanation: Universal group membership replicates to every global catalog, so nesting stable global groups in the universal groups keeps frequent changes inside each domain's global groups. Domain local groups can't be granted permissions outside their own domain. Universal group membership caching reduces sign-in lookups, not replication, and distribution groups can't be used for permissions.

prompt: A department manager must be able to add and remove members of the Marketing-Share group without receiving any other permissions in AD DS. What is the simplest way to achieve this?

options.text: Add the manager to the Account Operators group
On the group's Managed By tab, select the manager and enable Manager can update membership list
Run the Delegation of Control Wizard on the domain and delegate Create, delete, and manage groups
Add the manager to the Group Policy Creator Owners group

explanation: Setting Managed By with Manager can update membership list grants the manager write access to that group's membership only. Account Operators is a highly privileged built-in group, and delegating group management at the domain grants rights over every group. Group Policy Creator Owners lets members create GPOs, not manage group membership.

prompt: A GPO linked to the domain sets Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit to 600 seconds. A GPO linked to the Servers OU sets it to 1800 seconds, and servers receive 1800. Security requires the domain value on all servers, and the OU GPO must not be edited. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Set the domain GPO's link to Enforced
Enable Block Inheritance on the Servers OU
Change the link order on the Servers OU so the domain GPO is processed first
Enable loopback processing in Merge mode in the domain GPO

explanation: GPOs apply in local, site, domain, OU order and later GPOs win conflicts, but an enforced link makes its settings win over GPOs linked lower in the hierarchy. Block Inheritance would stop the domain GPO from applying at all. Link order on the OU orders only GPOs linked to that OU, and loopback processing affects user settings.

prompt: The Research OU has Block Inheritance enabled. A domain-linked GPO that configures Windows Firewall must still apply to computers in Research, while other domain-linked GPOs should stay blocked. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Disable Block Inheritance on the Research OU
Link the firewall GPO to the site that contains the Research computers
Set the firewall GPO's domain link to Enforced
Add a WMI filter to the firewall GPO that targets Research computers

explanation: Block Inheritance can't block an enforced link, so enforcing only the firewall GPO's link delivers it to Research while other domain GPOs stay blocked. Removing Block Inheritance would let every domain GPO through. Site-linked GPOs are also blocked unless enforced, and a WMI filter only narrows a GPO that is already delivered.

prompt: An administrator changed the security filtering of a GPO that contains user settings, removing Authenticated Users and adding the group HR-Users. Now the GPO doesn't apply to anyone, and gpresult reports it as inaccessible. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add HR-Users to the Group Policy Creator Owners group
Link the GPO to the domain instead of the OU
Enable loopback processing in Replace mode in a GPO linked to the computers' OU
Grant Authenticated Users or Domain Computers Read permission on the GPO

explanation: Since the MS16-072 update, user policies are retrieved in the computer's security context, so computers need Read access to the GPO; granting Authenticated Users or Domain Computers Read, without Apply, fixes it while HR-Users keeps Apply. Group Policy Creator Owners lets users create GPOs. Linking elsewhere or enabling loopback doesn't give computers read access.

prompt: A GPO linked to the Servers OU must apply only to servers running Windows Server 2025, but the OU also contains Windows Server 2022 servers, and the administrator doesn't want to reorganize the OU. What should be used?

options.text: Item-level targeting on the GPO
A WMI filter linked to the GPO that checks the operating system version
Security filtering that uses the Domain Computers group
Block Inheritance on the Servers OU

explanation: A WMI filter can query properties such as Win32_OperatingSystem's version and apply the GPO only when the query returns true. Item-level targeting applies to individual Group Policy preference items, not whole GPOs or policy settings. Domain Computers contains every computer, and Block Inheritance blocks parent GPOs rather than filtering this one.

prompt: Users sign in to Remote Desktop Session Host servers in the RDS-Servers OU. While on those servers, users must receive only the user settings from a GPO linked to RDS-Servers and none from GPOs linked to their own user OUs. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Loopback processing in Merge mode in a GPO linked to the users' OUs
Block Inheritance on the users' OUs
Loopback processing in Replace mode in a GPO linked to RDS-Servers
Security filtering on the RDS-Servers GPO for the Domain Users group

explanation: Loopback processing in Replace mode applies the user settings from GPOs in the computer's scope and ignores the user's normal GPOs. Merge mode combines both sets, with the computer's GPOs winning only on conflicts, and loopback must be configured in a GPO that applies to the computers. Block Inheritance on the user OUs doesn't change where users get settings on the RDS servers.

prompt: Several administrators edit GPOs from different workstations and see different Administrative Templates settings because their local ADMX files differ. What should be done so all administrators use the same templates?

options.text: Copy the ADMX and ADML files to a PolicyDefinitions folder in the domain's SYSVOL
Copy the same ADMX and ADML files to each administrator's %windir%\PolicyDefinitions folder
Import the ADMX files into a Starter GPO
Run gpupdate /force on every domain controller

explanation: When a PolicyDefinitions folder exists in the domain's SYSVOL Policies folder, the Group Policy editors use it as a central store for every administrator, and it replicates to all DCs. Copying files to each workstation still allows drift. Starter GPOs hold settings, not ADMX template files, and gpupdate refreshes policy without changing templates.

prompt: An administrator needs to find out which GPO actually applied a specific security setting to server SRV07 during its last policy refresh, without signing in to the server. Which Group Policy Management Console feature should be used?

options.text: Group Policy Modeling
Get-GPOReport for every GPO in the domain
Starter GPOs
Group Policy Results

explanation: Group Policy Results gathers the resultant set of policy from the target computer and user and shows the winning GPO for each setting. Group Policy Modeling simulates a hypothetical scenario instead of reporting what applied. Get-GPOReport reports each GPO's configured settings, not which one won on a computer, and Starter GPOs are templates.

prompt: Before moving several users into a new OU, an administrator wants to see which policy settings they would receive after the move, without moving them yet. What should be used?

options.text: Group Policy Results
Group Policy Modeling
gpresult /r on one of the users' computers
Invoke-GPUpdate on the users' computers

explanation: Group Policy Modeling simulates the settings users and computers would receive in a specified location, including an OU they aren't in yet. Group Policy Results and gpresult report what has already applied in the current location. Invoke-GPUpdate refreshes policy rather than predicting it.

prompt: An administrator tested a GPO in the test.contoso.com domain and wants to copy its settings into an empty GPO in the separate prod.fabrikam.com forest, translating the test domain's security groups to production groups. Which approach should be used?

options.text: Copy the GPO's folder from the test domain's SYSVOL into the production domain's SYSVOL folder
Run Restore-GPO in prod.fabrikam.com against a backup of the test GPO
Back up the GPO and import it into prod.fabrikam.com with Import-GPO and a migration table
Link the test GPO to the production domain by using New-GPLink

explanation: Import-GPO copies settings from a GPO backup into a GPO in any domain and can use a migration table to translate security principals and UNC paths. Restore-GPO restores a GPO only to its original domain. Copying SYSVOL folders doesn't create the matching AD objects, and GPOs can't be linked across forests.

prompt: An administrator must trigger an immediate Group Policy refresh on every server in the Servers OU from a management workstation, without restarting the servers. Which approach should be used?

options.text: Pipe Get-ADComputer results for the OU to Invoke-GPUpdate -Force
Pipe Get-ADComputer results for the OU to Set-GPLink -Enforced Yes
Run Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy for each server and save the HTML reports
Pipe Get-ADComputer results for the OU to Restart-Computer -Force

explanation: Invoke-GPUpdate schedules a remote policy refresh on each target computer, as does the Group Policy Update option on an OU in GPMC. Set-GPLink changes the properties of a GPO link on a container and doesn't refresh policy. Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy only produces reports, and restarting would apply policy but violates the no-restart requirement.

prompt: An administrator wants every new GPO created for branch servers to start with the same set of Administrative Templates settings already configured. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A WMI filter
A migration table
A GPO backup
A Starter GPO

explanation: A Starter GPO stores a baseline of Administrative Templates settings that is copied into each new GPO created from it. WMI filters control where a GPO applies, migration tables translate principals during import or copy, and a backup is used for restore or import rather than as a template.

prompt: A Group Policy preference maps drive S: to \\fs1\sales. Users sometimes change the mapping's settings, and the administrator wants each refresh to delete the existing mapping and recreate it exactly as configured. Which action should the preference item use?

options.text: Create
Replace
Update
Delete

explanation: Replace deletes the existing item and creates it again, so each refresh resets it to the configured state. Create adds the item only if it doesn't exist, Update changes only the configured properties of an existing item and creates it if it's missing, and Delete removes the mapping.

prompt: One GPO must map drive P: to the Projects share only for members of the Project-Team group, and drive F: to the Finance share only for members of the Finance group. Which feature allows this within a single GPO?

options.text: Security filtering on the GPO
A WMI filter on the GPO
Item-level targeting on each drive map preference item
Loopback processing in Merge mode for the users' computers

explanation: Item-level targeting filters individual preference items by criteria such as security group membership, so each drive map applies only to its group. Security filtering and WMI filters apply to the whole GPO, so they can't target the two drive maps separately. Loopback processing changes where user settings come from, not which users receive an item.

prompt: A drive map preference should be removed from users' sessions automatically when those users move out of the GPO's scope. Which preference option should be enabled?

options.text: Remove this item when it is no longer applied
Apply once and do not reapply
Run in logged-on user's security context
Stop processing items in this extension if an error occurs

explanation: Remove this item when it is no longer applied deletes the item once the GPO stops applying to the user, and it requires the Replace action. Apply once and do not reapply processes the item a single time, the security context option sets the identity used to apply the item, and the stop-processing option affects behavior after an error.

prompt: An administrator uses a registry preference to set a default application value on servers. Local administrators must be able to change the value afterward without Group Policy setting it back. Which preference option should be enabled?

options.text: Remove this item when it is no longer applied
Item-level targeting by organizational unit
Run in logged-on user's security context
Apply once and do not reapply

explanation: Apply once and do not reapply writes the value a single time, so later local changes aren't overwritten at the next refresh. Removing the item when it no longer applies relates to scope changes, item-level targeting decides which computers receive the item, and the security context option controls the account used to apply it.

prompt: An administrator needs a unique, regularly rotated password for the built-in local Administrator account on every member server. A colleague suggests the Local Users and Groups preference. What should the administrator do instead?

options.text: Use the Local Users and Groups preference and protect the cpassword value with the domain key
Deploy Windows LAPS and configure it through Group Policy to back up passwords to AD DS
Use a Restricted Groups policy to set the local Administrator password
Set the local Administrator password in the Default Domain Policy

explanation: Windows LAPS generates a unique password for each device, rotates it and backs it up to AD DS or Microsoft Entra ID. Group Policy preferences can no longer store passwords because the cpassword value was encrypted with a publicly known key (MS14-025). Restricted Groups controls group membership, not passwords, and the Default Domain Policy password settings don't set a local account's password.

prompt: The Windows Admin Center extension is installed on an Azure Arc-enabled Windows Server. A help desk engineer who has the Reader role on the server resource must be able to connect to it by using Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal. Which additional Azure role should the engineer receive on the server resource?

options.text: Virtual Machine Administrator Login
Azure Connected Machine Onboarding
Windows Admin Center Administrator Login
Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator

explanation: Connecting to Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal requires Reader plus Windows Admin Center Administrator Login on the Arc-enabled server. Virtual Machine Administrator Login is for Microsoft Entra sign-in to Azure VMs. The Azure Connected Machine Onboarding and Resource Administrator roles cover onboarding and managing Arc resources, not a Windows Admin Center connection.

prompt: Security policy forbids opening any inbound firewall ports to on-premises servers. An administrator wants to manage the servers' roles, files and event logs from the Azure portal, and the servers are already connected to Azure Arc. What is required?

options.text: Install the Windows Admin Center extension and allow outbound HTTPS to the required Azure endpoints
Install the Windows Admin Center extension and open its port inbound from the internet
Assign each server a public IP address and publish it through a reverse proxy
Deploy a site-to-site VPN so that the Azure portal can reach the servers

explanation: Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal uses the Arc agent to set up an outbound reverse proxy session, so only outbound HTTPS to the documented endpoints is needed. No inbound port, public IP address or VPN is required for the connection.

prompt: An administrator uses a Windows Admin Center gateway installed on SRV-MGMT to manage 40 servers. SRV-MGMT is Arc-enabled, and the administrator is considering enabling Windows Admin Center for it in the Azure portal. What should the administrator be aware of?

options.text: The portal version runs side by side with the existing gateway on a separate port
The existing gateway automatically publishes all 40 managed servers as Arc resources in the Azure portal
The Azure Arc agent must be uninstalled before the portal version can be enabled
Enabling it replaces the existing installation and removes its ability to manage other servers

explanation: Installing Windows Admin Center from the Azure portal on a machine that already has a manually installed instance replaces that instance and removes its ability to manage other machines. It doesn't run side by side or publish other servers, and it depends on the Arc agent rather than requiring its removal.

prompt: Windows Admin Center runs as a gateway service on SRV-WAC. When administrators connect through it to SRV-FS1, they're prompted for credentials again and some tools fail with access denied. The administrator wants the gateway to pass the signed-in user's Kerberos credentials to managed servers. What should be configured?

options.text: Enable CredSSP on SRV-WAC and on every managed server, and allow delegating fresh credentials
Configure resource-based Kerberos constrained delegation from each managed server to SRV-WAC
Add SRV-WAC's computer account to the Protected Users group
Add all administrators to the Windows Admin Center Gateway users role

explanation: Single sign-on through a Windows Admin Center gateway uses resource-based Kerberos constrained delegation, set with Set-ADComputer -PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount on each managed server. CredSSP sends reusable credentials and isn't the recommended approach. Protected Users is meant for user accounts and blocks delegation, and the Gateway users role controls access to the gateway, not delegation.

prompt: Help desk staff must be able to use a Windows Admin Center gateway to connect to servers but must not be able to change the gateway's settings or access control. How should access be configured in Windows Admin Center?

options.text: Add the help desk group to Gateway administrators
Add the help desk group to the local Administrators group on the gateway server
Add the help desk group to Gateway users
Add the help desk group to the Remote Desktop Users group on the gateway server

explanation: Gateway users can connect through the gateway to manage servers, subject to their permissions on those servers, while Gateway administrators can also change gateway settings and access. Local administrators of the gateway server always have gateway administrator rights. Remote Desktop Users governs RDP sign-in, not Windows Admin Center access.

prompt: From a domain-joined management server, an administrator runs Enter-PSSession against a workgroup server by IP address with a local administrator account on that server. The connection fails with an error about Kerberos and TrustedHosts. What should the administrator do on the management server?

options.text: Add the workgroup server's IP address to WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts
Run Enable-PSRemoting -SkipNetworkProfileCheck on the management server
Add the workgroup server to the domain's Remote Management Users group
Configure resource-based Kerberos constrained delegation for the workgroup server

explanation: When Kerberos can't be used, as with a workgroup computer or an IP address, WinRM requires the remote computer to be in the client's TrustedHosts list or an HTTPS listener. Enabling remoting on the management server doesn't change client trust settings. A workgroup computer can't be added to a domain group, and Kerberos delegation requires both computers to be in AD DS.

prompt: An administrator connects from a workstation to SRV-B with Enter-PSSession and runs a command that reads a file from a share on SRV-C. The command fails with access denied. The administrator must fix this without sending reusable credentials to SRV-B. What should be configured?

options.text: Enable CredSSP on the workstation and on SRV-B
Configure unconstrained delegation on the SRV-B computer account
Add the administrator's account to the Protected Users group
Set PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount on SRV-C's computer object to include SRV-B

explanation: This is the second-hop problem; resource-based Kerberos constrained delegation, configured on SRV-C, lets SRV-B delegate the user's Kerberos credentials without holding reusable credentials. CredSSP solves the problem but caches the user's credentials on SRV-B. Unconstrained delegation is a serious security risk, and members of Protected Users can't be delegated at all.

prompt: An administrator is building a Just Enough Administration (JEA) endpoint so that DNS operators can only restart the DNS service and clear the DNS server cache. In which file should the allowed cmdlets and functions be defined?

options.text: A session configuration file (.pssc)
A role capability file (.psrc)
A module manifest file (.psd1)
A session transcript file

explanation: A role capability file lists the cmdlets, functions, parameters and external commands visible to a role. The session configuration file defines the endpoint, maps users or groups to role capabilities and sets options such as a virtual account. A module manifest describes a module, and transcripts record sessions rather than defining permissions.

prompt: An administrator created a JEA session configuration file named DnsOps.pssc and placed the role capability file in a module folder. Which command makes the JEA endpoint available to users?

options.text: New-PSSessionConfigurationFile -Path .\DnsOps.pssc
Enable-PSRemoting -Force
Register-PSSessionConfiguration -Name DnsOps -Path .\DnsOps.pssc
Import-Module -Name DnsOps

explanation: Register-PSSessionConfiguration creates the endpoint from the .pssc file. New-PSSessionConfigurationFile only creates a configuration file, Enable-PSRemoting turns on WinRM and the default endpoints, and Import-Module loads a module into the current session without creating an endpoint.

prompt: A JEA endpoint named DnsOps is registered on SRV-DNS1. How should an operator connect to it from a workstation?

options.text: Enter-PSSession -ComputerName SRV-DNS1 -ConfigurationName DnsOps
Enter-PSSession -VMName SRV-DNS1 -ConfigurationName DnsOps
Enter-PSSession -HostName SRV-DNS1 -Subsystem DnsOps
Enter-PSSession -ComputerName SRV-DNS1 -Authentication CredSSP

explanation: A JEA endpoint is reached over WinRM by naming its session configuration with -ConfigurationName. -VMName uses PowerShell Direct from a Hyper-V host, -HostName with -Subsystem uses SSH remoting and an SSH subsystem rather than a JEA endpoint, and the CredSSP option connects to the default endpoint and delegates credentials instead of restricting the session.

prompt: Auditors require a record of every command run by operators who connect to a JEA endpoint. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Windows Firewall logging for WinRM traffic
RunAsVirtualAccount set to $true in the session configuration file
Membership of the operators in the Event Log Readers group
TranscriptDirectory in the session configuration file

explanation: The TranscriptDirectory setting makes JEA save an over-the-shoulder transcript of each session, including the commands run. Firewall logs record connections, not commands. RunAsVirtualAccount sets the identity that commands run as, and Event Log Readers allows reading logs instead of creating an audit trail.

prompt: An administrator wants a new Windows Server 2025 server to accept SSH connections. What is the simplest way to do this?

options.text: Download Win32-OpenSSH from GitHub and run install-sshd.ps1
Enable Remote SSH Access in Server Manager, which starts the preinstalled sshd service
Run Add-WindowsCapability to install OpenSSH Server, because it isn't included in Windows Server 2025
Install the Remote Desktop Services role, which provides the SSH listener

explanation: In Windows Server 2025, the OpenSSH server component is installed by default, and Server Manager includes a Remote SSH Access option that enables the sshd service. A GitHub download or capability install isn't needed, and the claim that the component isn't included is wrong. Remote Desktop Services provides RDP, not SSH.

prompt: An administrator set up key-based SSH authentication on a Windows Server for an account that belongs to the local Administrators group. The public key is in C:\Users\admin1\.ssh\authorized_keys, but key authentication fails, while a standard user's key works. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Move the key into C:\Users\admin1\.ssh\known_hosts and restart the sshd service
Store the public key under the HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH registry key and restart the sshd service
Put the key in C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys with a restricted ACL
Disable User Account Control on the server

explanation: The default Windows sshd_config reads %ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys for members of Administrators, and that file must be accessible only to Administrators and SYSTEM. known_hosts stores server host keys on a client, OpenSSH doesn't read public keys from the registry, and disabling UAC doesn't change which key file sshd uses.

prompt: An administrator wants to use PowerShell 7 remoting over SSH to manage Windows Server and Linux servers from the same script. Which New-PSSession parameter specifies an SSH-based connection?

options.text: -HostName
-ComputerName
-VMName
-UseSSL

explanation: With -HostName, optionally with -UserName or -KeyFilePath, PowerShell uses SSH as the transport. -ComputerName uses WinRM, -VMName uses PowerShell Direct through the Hyper-V host and -UseSSL makes a WinRM connection use HTTPS.

prompt: An administrator wants to SSH to an Azure Arc-enabled server through Azure without opening any inbound port on the corporate firewall. The Arc agent is connected. What must be configured on the server's Arc agent?

options.text: azcmagent config set extensions.allowlist with the SSH extension name
azcmagent connect with a new service principal
azcmagent check with the SSH endpoint as the location
azcmagent config set incomingconnections.ports 22

explanation: SSH access through Azure Arc relies on the agent's outbound connection, but the agent must allow the local port through incomingconnections.ports so the proxied session can reach sshd. The extension allowlist controls which VM extensions may be installed, azcmagent connect onboards a machine and azcmagent check tests connectivity to Azure endpoints.

prompt: Security policy requires that users who connect to servers by using Remote Desktop authenticate before the server creates a full remote session and sign-in screen. What should be enabled?

options.text: RD Gateway with HTTP transport
Restricted Admin mode
Network Level Authentication
Membership in the Remote Desktop Users group

explanation: Network Level Authentication requires the user to authenticate before the server builds the full session, which uses fewer resources and reduces exposure to denial-of-service attacks. RD Gateway publishes RDP across the internet, Restricted Admin mode avoids sending reusable credentials to the target and Remote Desktop Users controls who may connect.

prompt: A developer who isn't an administrator needs to connect to member server SRV-APP1 with Remote Desktop, which is already enabled on the server. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Add the developer to the Remote Management Users group on SRV-APP1
Add the developer to the Remote Desktop Users group on SRV-APP1
Add the developer to the Server Operators group in the domain
Add the developer to the Network Configuration Operators group on SRV-APP1

explanation: On member servers, the Remote Desktop Users group has the Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services right. Remote Management Users grants WinRM access, Server Operators is a privileged group that applies to domain controllers, and Network Configuration Operators can only change network settings.

prompt: An administrator needs to enable Remote Desktop on a Server Core installation by using PowerShell. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Set the fDenyTSConnections registry value to 0 and enable the Remote Desktop firewall rules
Run Enable-PSRemoting -Force and restart the WinRM service
Install the Remote Desktop Session Host role service and restart the server so the listener starts
Set the startup type of the TermService service to Automatic

explanation: Setting fDenyTSConnections to 0 under HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server allows RDP connections, and enabling the Remote Desktop firewall rule group with Enable-NetFirewallRule lets them through; SConfig offers the same option. Enable-PSRemoting configures WinRM, not RDP. The Session Host role is for multi-user RDS deployments, and changing the service startup type alone doesn't allow connections.

prompt: An administrator must onboard 300 on-premises Windows Servers to Azure Arc by using a script deployed through a configuration management tool, without interactive sign-in on each server. What should the administrator use?

options.text: A user account with the Owner role, signing in with device code each time azcmagent connect runs
A service principal with the Azure Connected Machine Onboarding role, used by azcmagent connect
An Azure VM's managed identity assigned the Reader role
The Windows Admin Center extension installed on each server

explanation: For onboarding at scale, Microsoft recommends a service principal with the Azure Connected Machine Onboarding role, passed to azcmagent connect in the generated script. Device code sign-in is interactive on each server. An Azure VM's managed identity can't be used by on-premises servers to onboard, and the Windows Admin Center extension requires a machine that is already Arc-enabled.

prompt: A company's on-premises servers must connect to Azure Arc over ExpressRoute private peering, and the Arc agent traffic must not use public endpoints. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An Azure Bastion host in the hub virtual network
A Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on the gateway subnet
Create an Azure Arc Private Link Scope with a private endpoint and private DNS for the Arc endpoints
Configure the Arc agent's proxy setting to send traffic through the ExpressRoute gateway's IP address

explanation: An Azure Arc Private Link Scope lets Arc-enabled servers reach Arc services through private endpoints over ExpressRoute or VPN, with DNS resolving the endpoints to private IP addresses. Bastion provides RDP and SSH to Azure VMs, a storage service endpoint doesn't cover Arc services, and an ExpressRoute gateway isn't an HTTP proxy.

prompt: Before onboarding a server to Azure Arc, an administrator wants to confirm that the server can reach all the required Azure endpoints through the corporate proxy. Which command should be run after the Connected Machine agent is installed?

options.text: azcmagent check
azcmagent show
azcmagent logs
azcmagent disconnect

explanation: azcmagent check tests connectivity from the machine to the network endpoints the agent requires. azcmagent show displays the agent's connection status and services, azcmagent logs collects log files for troubleshooting and azcmagent disconnect removes the machine's connection to Azure.

prompt: Every current and future Azure Arc-enabled Windows Server in a subscription must run the Azure Monitor agent and send data according to a specific data collection rule. What is the most efficient approach?

options.text: Install the Log Analytics agent manually on each server and connect it to a workspace
Use the Custom Script Extension on each server to install the agent
Use Windows Admin Center to install the agent on each server
Assign Azure Policy to deploy the Azure Monitor agent and associate the DCR

explanation: Built-in Azure Policy definitions can deploy the Azure Monitor agent extension and the data collection rule (DCR) association to Arc-enabled servers, covering new servers automatically and remediating existing ones. The Log Analytics agent is retired. A Custom Script Extension or Windows Admin Center would require work on each server and wouldn't cover future servers on their own.

prompt: An administrator needs to run a PowerShell script that sets a registry value on several Azure Arc-enabled servers, started from Azure with the result shown in the Azure portal. Which VM extension should be used?

options.text: Azure Monitor agent extension
Custom Script Extension
Azure Key Vault extension
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint extension

explanation: The Custom Script Extension downloads and runs scripts on Arc-enabled servers and reports the outcome in Azure. The Azure Monitor agent collects monitoring data, the Key Vault extension refreshes certificates from Key Vault and the Defender for Endpoint extension onboards the endpoint protection sensor.

prompt: A security team wants only the Azure Monitor agent and Microsoft Defender extensions to be installable on a group of Arc-enabled servers, even by Azure administrators who have permission to deploy extensions. What should be configured on each server?

options.text: An Azure Policy assignment with the deny effect on the resource group
azcmagent config set incomingconnections.ports
azcmagent config set extensions.allowlist with the permitted extensions
A Windows Firewall rule that blocks the extension service

explanation: The Connected Machine agent's local extensions.allowlist setting restricts which extensions can be installed, and only a local administrator on the machine can change it. An Azure Policy assignment can be changed by sufficiently privileged Azure administrators, so it isn't local enforcement. incomingconnections.ports controls ports for remote access features, and blocking the extension service would also stop the permitted extensions.

prompt: A web application runs on an Arc-enabled Windows Server. Its TLS certificate is stored in Azure Key Vault and is renewed there automatically. The renewed certificate must be installed on the server automatically. What should be deployed?

options.text: The Custom Script Extension with a one-time import script
The Azure Monitor agent with a data collection rule
The Windows Admin Center extension
The Azure Key Vault VM extension

explanation: The Key Vault VM extension, which is supported on Arc-enabled servers, regularly retrieves certificates from Key Vault and installs renewed versions in the local certificate store. A one-time script doesn't pick up later renewals. The Azure Monitor agent and Windows Admin Center extensions don't manage Key Vault certificates.

prompt: An administrator must continuously audit whether Arc-enabled Windows Servers comply with required OS settings, such as password and audit policies, and report compliance in Azure. What should be used?

options.text: Azure Policy with machine configuration policy definitions
Azure Update Manager periodic assessment
Microsoft Defender for Servers just-in-time VM access
Azure Automation runbooks scheduled to run every hour

explanation: Azure Machine Configuration, formerly guest configuration, works through Azure Policy to audit and optionally configure settings inside the operating systems of Azure and Arc-enabled machines and reports compliance. Update Manager assesses missing updates, just-in-time access controls management ports and a runbook would require custom code and reporting.

prompt: An administrator uses Azure Machine Configuration to deploy a custom configuration to Arc-enabled servers. If a local administrator changes one of the managed settings, it must be reset automatically. Which assignment type should be used?

options.text: Audit
ApplyAndMonitor
ApplyAndAutoCorrect
DeployIfNotExists

explanation: ApplyAndAutoCorrect applies the configuration and corrects drift whenever it's detected. Audit only reports compliance and ApplyAndMonitor applies the configuration once and then only reports drift. DeployIfNotExists is an Azure Policy effect, not a machine configuration assignment type.

prompt: A company runs Windows Server 2025 Datacenter on physical on-premises servers and wants to install monthly security updates without restarting the servers whenever possible. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Configure Cluster-Aware Updating on each standalone server
Connect the servers to Azure Arc and enable Hotpatch for them
Enable automatic VM guest patching in Azure Update Manager
Deploy the updates through Windows Server Update Services with installation deadlines
