Kerberos armoring enabled in the Default Domain Controllers Policy

explanation: A KDC proxy forwards Kerberos requests from clients to domain controllers over HTTPS, so internet clients can obtain tickets; clients are pointed at it with the Specify KDC proxy servers for Kerberos clients policy. Exposing a DC to the internet is a security risk, SMB signing doesn't change the authentication protocol and Kerberos armoring still requires that clients reach a KDC.

prompt: A share containing payroll files must be encrypted in transit for every client connection, while other shares on the same server don't need encryption. Which command should be run?

options.text: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EncryptData $true
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true
Set-SmbClientConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true
Set-SmbShare -Name Payroll -EncryptData $true

explanation: Set-SmbShare -EncryptData $true turns on SMB encryption for that share only. Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EncryptData encrypts every share on the server, and the signing settings protect integrity without encrypting data.

prompt: A vulnerability scan reports that SMB 1.0 is enabled on several older file servers. Which command disables the SMB 1.0 server protocol?

options.text: Set-SmbClientConfiguration -EnableInsecureGuestLogons $false
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB2Protocol $false
Set-SmbShare -Name Data -FolderEnumerationMode AccessBased

explanation: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false turns off the SMB 1.0 server, and removing the SMB 1.0 feature removes it entirely. Insecure guest logons are a client setting, disabling SMB2 also disables SMB 3 and breaks modern clients and FolderEnumerationMode controls access-based enumeration.

prompt: After a server is upgraded to Windows Server 2025, a script on it can no longer copy files to an older third-party NAS that doesn't support SMB signing. Copies to Windows file servers still work. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: SMB signing is now required by default on all outbound SMB connections
SMB encryption is now required on all inbound SMB connections
The SMB authentication rate limiter is blocking the NAS
SMB over QUIC replaced TCP as the default SMB transport

explanation: In Windows Server 2025, the SMB client requires signing on all outbound connections by default, so connections to a device that can't sign fail. Encryption isn't required on inbound connections by default, the authentication rate limiter delays failed NTLM authentication attempts against an SMB server and Windows SMB clients still use TCP by default.

prompt: An administrator adds a new 8 TB disk to a server and must create a single 8 TB volume on it. How should the disk be initialized?

options.text: MBR, because data disks require it
MBR, and then convert the disk to dynamic
GPT
MBR with an extended partition

explanation: MBR partitions are limited to 2 TB, so a single 8 TB volume requires a GPT disk. Converting an MBR disk to dynamic is deprecated for most uses and still doesn't allow one 8 TB volume on that disk, and an extended partition doesn't remove the MBR limit.

prompt: A server has three identical HDDs for an archive storage pool. The archive must survive one drive failure, and usable capacity matters more than write performance. Which resiliency type should the virtual disk use?

options.text: Parity
Simple
Two-way mirror
Three-way mirror

explanation: Single parity tolerates one drive failure with three or more drives and provides more usable capacity than mirroring, at the cost of write performance. Simple has no resiliency, a two-way mirror survives one failure but uses half the raw capacity and a three-way mirror needs at least five drives.

prompt: An administrator created a four-node failover cluster from servers with local NVMe and SSD drives and validated it with Test-Cluster, including the Storage Spaces Direct tests. Which cmdlet turns on Storage Spaces Direct?

options.text: New-StoragePool
Add-ClusterSharedVolume
New-SRPartnership
Enable-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect

explanation: Enable-ClusterStorageSpacesDirect claims the eligible local drives, creates the pool, configures the cache and sets up storage tiers. New-StoragePool creates a pool on a standalone server, Add-ClusterSharedVolume adds an existing clustered disk to CSV and New-SRPartnership configures Storage Replica.

prompt: A branch office is deploying a two-node Storage Spaces Direct cluster. What must the administrator configure so that the cluster keeps running if one node fails?

options.text: A third node, because Storage Spaces Direct needs at least three nodes
A cluster witness, such as a cloud witness or a file share witness
Storage Replica between the two nodes
A three-way mirror volume across the two nodes

explanation: A two-node cluster needs a witness so that a quorum majority survives when one node is down, and a cloud or file share witness is commonly used. Storage Spaces Direct supports two-node clusters, Storage Replica isn't used to protect S2D within a cluster and a three-way mirror requires at least three servers.

prompt: Two datacenters 20 km apart are connected by a link with less than 5 ms round-trip latency. A volume must be replicated between them with no data loss if the primary site fails. Which configuration should be used?

options.text: Storage Replica with asynchronous replication
Hyper-V Replica with a 30-second replication frequency
Storage Replica with synchronous replication
DFS Replication with a large staging quota

explanation: Synchronous Storage Replica acknowledges each write only after it's committed at both sites, giving zero data loss over low-latency links. Asynchronous replication and Hyper-V Replica can lose the most recent writes, and DFS Replication copies files rather than replicating volumes at the block level.

prompt: Before creating a Storage Replica partnership between two servers, an administrator wants to confirm that the network, log volume and performance meet the requirements. Which cmdlet should be run?

options.text: Test-SRTopology
Get-SRGroup
Test-Cluster
Get-SRPartnership

explanation: Test-SRTopology measures the environment over a period and produces a report that covers prerequisites, network performance and log volume sizing. Get-SRGroup and Get-SRPartnership display existing configurations, and Test-Cluster validates failover clusters rather than server-to-server replication readiness.

prompt: A company wants to use Storage Replica on Windows Server 2025 Standard edition to replicate a volume between two servers. Which limitation applies?

options.text: Storage Replica isn't available in Standard edition
Only asynchronous replication is supported in Standard edition
Only stretch cluster replication is supported in Standard edition
One volume of up to 2 TB in a single partnership

explanation: Standard edition includes Storage Replica with limits: one replicated volume of up to 2 TB in a single partnership, while Datacenter has no such limits. Both synchronous and asynchronous replication are available, and server-to-server replication isn't restricted to stretch clusters.

prompt: An administrator is enabling Data Deduplication on a volume that stores the VHDX files of running virtual desktops in a VDI deployment. Which usage type should be selected?

options.text: Default (general purpose file server)
Hyper-V
Backup
Storage Replica

explanation: The Hyper-V usage type is tuned for VDI workloads and optimizes open VHDX files. Default is for general-purpose file servers, Backup is for virtualized backup applications and Storage Replica is a replication feature, not a deduplication usage type.

prompt: An administrator wants to confirm that the network adapters on a Hyper-V host can use SMB Direct to reach a Scale-Out File Server. Which command shows whether RDMA is enabled on the adapters?

options.text: Get-NetAdapterRss
Get-NetLbfoTeam
Get-NetAdapterRdma
Get-SmbShare

explanation: Get-NetAdapterRdma shows whether RDMA is enabled on each adapter, and Get-SmbClientNetworkInterface shows whether SMB sees an interface as RDMA capable. RSS spreads receive processing across CPUs, LBFO teams don't support RDMA and Get-SmbShare lists shares.

prompt: Ten VMs that belong to one tenant are stored on a Scale-Out File Server and must be limited to 5,000 IOPS in total, shared among them. Which Storage QoS policy should be created?

options.text: A Dedicated policy with a maximum of 500 IOPS applied to each VM
A Dedicated policy with a maximum of 5,000 IOPS applied to each VM
A Hyper-V resource metering pool for the ten VMs
An Aggregated policy with a maximum of 5,000 IOPS applied to the ten VMs

explanation: An Aggregated policy shares its minimum and maximum across all the virtual disks it's applied to, so the ten VMs together are capped at 5,000 IOPS. A Dedicated policy applies the limits to each virtual disk separately, so 500 each prevents a busy VM from using idle capacity and 5,000 each allows up to 50,000. Resource metering reports usage but doesn't limit it.

prompt: A data volume must support NTFS disk quotas and Encrypting File System (EFS) for an existing application. Which file system should be used?

options.text: NTFS
ReFS
ReFS with integrity streams enabled
exFAT

explanation: NTFS supports disk quotas and EFS, neither of which ReFS supports, with or without integrity streams. exFAT lacks NTFS features such as ACL-based permissions, quotas and EFS.

prompt: A server connects to an iSCSI target through two network adapters on separate subnets. If one path fails, I/O must continue on the other. What should be configured on the server?

options.text: An LBFO NIC team that combines the two iSCSI network adapters
Multipath I/O with iSCSI support and sessions over both paths
CHAP authentication on the iSCSI initiator
A Storage QoS policy that reserves IOPS on the iSCSI volume

explanation: Multipath I/O with iSCSI support provides path failover and load balancing for iSCSI sessions across several adapters. NIC teaming isn't supported for iSCSI storage paths, CHAP authenticates the initiator and Storage QoS manages VM performance on CSV storage.

prompt: An iSCSI Target Server must allow only authorized initiators to connect to a target, even if an attacker spoofs an allowed initiator's IQN. What should be configured?

options.text: Access by initiator IQN only
An iSCSI virtual disk stored on ReFS
CHAP authentication, optionally with reverse CHAP
SMB encryption on the target server

explanation: CHAP requires the initiator to prove knowledge of a shared secret, and reverse CHAP also authenticates the target, so a spoofed IQN alone isn't enough. IQN-based access can be bypassed by spoofing, the file system holding the virtual disk doesn't affect authentication and SMB encryption doesn't apply to iSCSI traffic.

prompt: An administrator runs manage-bde on a new Windows Server 2025 file server to encrypt a data volume, but BitLocker isn't available. What should the administrator do first?

options.text: Enable Credential Guard
Install the TPM driver from the hardware vendor
Enable Secure Boot through Group Policy
Install the BitLocker Drive Encryption feature

explanation: On Windows Server, BitLocker Drive Encryption is an optional feature that must be installed, for example with Install-WindowsFeature BitLocker -IncludeAllSubFeature -IncludeManagementTools, usually followed by a restart. Credential Guard is unrelated, TPM support is built into Windows and Secure Boot is configured in the firmware, not Group Policy.

prompt: Before encrypting server volumes, the administrator wants BitLocker recovery passwords stored in AD DS automatically, and encryption must not start until the recovery information is backed up. What should be configured?

options.text: The BitLocker policy to store recovery information in AD DS before enabling encryption
Windows LAPS with password backup to AD DS
A scheduled task that runs manage-bde -protectors -get and saves the output to a share
Credential Roaming through Group Policy

explanation: The BitLocker Group Policy settings for how drives can be recovered can save recovery passwords to AD DS and prevent BitLocker from turning on until the backup succeeds, and Backup-BitLockerKeyProtector can back up existing protectors. Windows LAPS manages local account passwords, a script that reads protectors doesn't guarantee backup before encryption and Credential Roaming synchronizes user certificates.

prompt: A BitLocker-encrypted data volume on a server is damaged and can't be unlocked normally. The administrator has the recovery password and wants to recover as much data as possible. Which tool should be used?

options.text: chkdsk /f on the encrypted volume
manage-bde -off to decrypt the damaged volume in place
repair-bde, writing the recovered data to another volume
Optimize-Volume -Defrag on the damaged volume

explanation: repair-bde reconstructs critical parts of a damaged BitLocker volume and writes the recovered data to a separate output volume by using a recovery password or key package. chkdsk and defragmentation can't work on an encrypted volume that won't unlock, and manage-bde -off needs an unlocked, readable volume.

prompt: An administrator configured exploit protection mitigations for a line-of-business application on a reference server and must apply the same settings to 200 servers through Group Policy. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Export with Set-ProcessMitigation -PolicyFilePath and import on each server with Get-ProcessMitigation
Add the application's path to the Attack surface reduction rules policy
Export the settings to XML and deploy it with the Use a common set of exploit protection settings policy
Enable Data Execution Prevention with bcdedit on each server

explanation: Exploit protection settings can be exported to an XML file, from Windows Security or with Get-ProcessMitigation -RegistryConfigFilePath, and deployed with the Use a common set of exploit protection settings policy. The first option reverses the cmdlets, because Set-ProcessMitigation -PolicyFilePath imports a file. ASR rules are a separate Defender feature, and bcdedit configures only system-wide DEP rather than per-application mitigations.

prompt: An administrator deployed an App Control for Business policy in audit mode to file servers. Before enforcing it, the administrator must find which binaries would have been blocked. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: Event ID 3076 in the Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational log
Event ID 4688 in the Security log
Event ID 8004 in the AppLocker EXE and DLL log
Event ID 1116 in the Microsoft Defender Antivirus operational log

explanation: In audit mode, App Control logs event 3076 in the CodeIntegrity Operational log for each file that would have been blocked, and event 3077 when an enforced policy blocks a file. Event 4688 records process creation, the AppLocker logs record AppLocker rule results and Defender event 1116 reports malware detections.

prompt: An organization is enforcing App Control for Business on servers. Only applications deployed by its software distribution tool should be allowed automatically, without adding rules for every new version. What should be configured?

options.text: A file path rule that allows C:\Program Files
Audit mode for the App Control policy on all servers
The Microsoft recommended driver block rules in the policy
The distribution tool's agent as a managed installer

explanation: Designating the deployment agent as a managed installer tags the files it writes, and an App Control policy with the managed installer option allows them. A path rule for Program Files would allow any file placed there, not only those from the tool. Audit mode enforces nothing, and the driver block rules deny known vulnerable drivers.

prompt: A security team asks whether Credential Guard must be enabled manually on new domain-joined Windows Server 2025 member servers that meet its hardware and virtualization-based security requirements. What is correct?

options.text: It can be turned on only through a Microsoft Intune endpoint security policy profile
It's on by default on Windows Server 2025 devices that meet the requirements
Credential Guard isn't available on Windows Server
It requires installing the Hyper-V server role on each server first

explanation: Starting with Windows Server 2025, Credential Guard is enabled by default on devices that meet its requirements, and it can also be managed with Group Policy or the registry. Intune isn't the only management method, Credential Guard is available on Windows Server and it relies on virtualization-based security rather than the Hyper-V server role.

prompt: Credential Guard isn't running on a physical server even though the policy to turn it on is applied, and System Information shows that virtualization-based security isn't running. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The server's computer account isn't in the Protected Users group
Windows Defender Firewall is turned off on the server
Virtualization extensions or Secure Boot are off in firmware
The server's NTLM audit policy is disabled

explanation: Credential Guard depends on virtualization-based security, which needs CPU virtualization extensions and Secure Boot to be available and enabled in the firmware. Protected Users is meant for user accounts, and the firewall state and NTLM auditing don't affect whether VBS can start.

prompt: On servers used for remote administration, users must be warned about unrecognized apps downloaded from the internet and must not be able to bypass the warning. What should be configured?

options.text: The SmartScreen policy in File Explorer, set to Warn and prevent bypass
An attack surface reduction rule for executable content from email
User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode
Windows Defender Firewall outbound block rules for web browsers

explanation: The Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen policy under Windows Components\File Explorer checks the reputation of downloaded apps and files, and Warn and prevent bypass stops users from continuing past the warning. The ASR rule targets email content, UAC controls elevation prompts and blocking browser traffic doesn't evaluate app reputation.

prompt: An administrator configured detailed audit subcategories under Advanced Audit Policy Configuration in a GPO, but servers still apply the legacy audit categories. Which additional security option should be enabled?

options.text: Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits
Audit: Audit the use of Backup and Restore privilege
Network security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic
Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings to override audit policy category settings

explanation: Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings to override audit policy category settings makes Windows apply the advanced subcategories instead of the legacy categories. Shutting down when audits can't be written, auditing backup privilege use and NTLM auditing don't change which audit policy model is used.

prompt: To limit lateral movement, local accounts on member servers must not be able to sign in through Remote Desktop, while domain administrators still can. Which Group Policy setting should be configured?

options.text: Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services, granted to the Administrators group
Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services, assigned to the Local account group
Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL
Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only

explanation: The Local account well-known group represents all local accounts, so assigning it to Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services blocks them from RDP without affecting domain accounts. Granting the right to Administrators would include local administrators. The CTRL+ALT+DEL and blank password settings don't block RDP for local accounts that have passwords.

prompt: An administrator wants to apply Microsoft's Windows Server 2025 security baseline to a domain-joined member server by using OSConfig. The Microsoft.OSConfig module is installed. Which command should be run?

options.text: Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/WorkgroupMember -Default
Get-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/MemberServer
Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/MemberServer -Default
Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/DomainController -Default

explanation: Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration with the MemberServer scenario and -Default applies the baseline for domain-joined member servers, followed by a restart. The WorkgroupMember and DomainController scenarios target other roles, and Get-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration only reports the baseline's settings and compliance.

prompt: After an OSConfig security baseline was applied to servers, one setting keeps switching between two values. The administrator finds that a GPO configures the same setting differently. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Manage the setting from only one source, or align the OSConfig value by using -Setting
Run gpupdate /force on the servers every hour so Group Policy wins the conflict
Uninstall the Microsoft.OSConfig module so drift control stops reapplying settings
Run Get-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration to reset the setting to its default

explanation: OSConfig protects baseline settings from drift, so when another tool such as Group Policy sets the same value differently, the two keep overwriting each other; Microsoft advises removing one source or customizing the OSConfig value with Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Setting. Frequent policy refreshes don't stop drift control, the supported way to remove a baseline is Remove-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration and the Get cmdlet only reads settings.

prompt: An administrator is deploying Windows LAPS with password backup to AD DS for member servers in the Servers OU. Which two PowerShell steps prepare Active Directory?

options.text: Run Update-LapsADSchema
Run Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission for the Servers OU
Run Add-KdsRootKey -EffectiveImmediately
Run Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -ComplexityEnabled $true
Run Reset-LapsPassword on a domain controller

explanation: Update-LapsADSchema adds the Windows LAPS attributes to the schema, and Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission grants computers in the OU permission to update their own password attributes. A KDS root key is used for gMSA passwords, the domain password policy doesn't prepare AD for LAPS and Reset-LapsPassword rotates the password on the device where it runs.

prompt: A help desk technician who has read permission on Windows LAPS passwords needs the current local administrator password of server SRV12 in plain text from PowerShell. Which command should be used?

options.text: Get-ADComputer SRV12 -Properties ms-Mcs-AdmPwd
Get-LapsADPassword -Identity SRV12 -AsPlainText
Reset-LapsPassword, run from the technician's workstation
Get-LapsDiagnostics -ComputerName SRV12

explanation: Get-LapsADPassword retrieves the Windows LAPS password stored in AD DS, and -AsPlainText shows it in readable form. ms-Mcs-AdmPwd is the legacy Microsoft LAPS attribute, Reset-LapsPassword rotates the password of the device it runs on rather than reading another server's password and Get-LapsDiagnostics collects troubleshooting logs.

prompt: An organization wants the Directory Services Restore Mode administrator password on each domain controller to be unique and rotated automatically. What should be used?

options.text: Windows LAPS configured to back up the DSRM account password to AD DS
Windows LAPS configured to back up the DSRM password to Microsoft Entra ID
A fine-grained password policy applied to the Domain Controllers group
A Group Policy preference that sets the Administrator password on DCs

explanation: Windows LAPS can manage the DSRM account on domain controllers, and that password can be backed up only to AD DS, not to Microsoft Entra ID. Fine-grained password policies apply to domain accounts rather than the DSRM account, and Group Policy preferences can no longer set passwords.

prompt: Windows Server 2025 member servers are sometimes restored from snapshots, after which administrators can't sign in with the Windows LAPS password stored in AD DS because the local password no longer matches. What should the administrator do so that Windows LAPS detects this and rotates the password automatically?

options.text: Shorten the PasswordAgeDays setting to one day
Configure a post-authentication action that resets the password
Update the schema with the latest Update-LapsADSchema
Set PasswordComplexity to 5 to use the readability dictionary

explanation: Image rollback detection uses the msLAPS-CurrentPasswordVersion attribute, which the latest Update-LapsADSchema adds; when the GUID in AD differs from the local copy, Windows LAPS rotates the password immediately. A shorter password age leaves the mismatch until the next rotation, post-authentication actions run after the password has been used and PasswordComplexity 5 only changes the character set.

prompt: A company enabled Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1 on a subscription and now needs file integrity monitoring for its servers. What must it do?

options.text: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 for the subscription
Install the Log Analytics agent on each server
Enable the Defender for Storage plan
Turn on the free foundational CSPM capabilities in Defender for Cloud

explanation: File integrity monitoring is included only in Defender for Servers Plan 2, which also adds features such as just-in-time VM access and agentless scanning. Defender for Servers no longer relies on the Log Analytics agent for most features, Defender for Storage protects storage accounts and foundational CSPM doesn't include file integrity monitoring.

prompt: An administrator wants Defender for Servers on only five servers in a large subscription, enabled per server rather than for the whole subscription. Which plan can be enabled at the resource level?

options.text: Plan 2 only
Both Plan 1 and Plan 2
Neither plan, because both must be enabled per subscription
Plan 1 only

explanation: Plan 1 can be enabled and disabled for individual servers, whereas Plan 2 can be enabled only for a subscription, although it can be disabled for specific resources. Microsoft still recommends enabling Defender for Servers at the subscription level.

prompt: A company wants Defender for Servers to protect its on-premises Windows Servers alongside its Azure VMs, with their security recommendations shown in Defender for Cloud. What should be done with the on-premises servers?

options.text: Install the Hybrid Runbook Worker extension on them
Join them to Microsoft Entra ID
Connect them to Azure Arc so that they appear as Azure resources
Add them to an Azure Update Manager maintenance configuration

explanation: On-premises machines are brought into Defender for Cloud by connecting them to Azure Arc, which gives them Azure resource representations that Defender for Servers can protect. Hybrid Runbook Workers run Automation jobs, Microsoft Entra join doesn't onboard servers to Defender for Cloud and Update Manager patches machines that are already Arc-enabled.

prompt: Servers that hold payroll data must accept connections only from computers that authenticate with IPsec, while domain controllers must stay reachable without IPsec so that authentication works. Which connection security rules should be created?

options.text: An isolation rule requiring authentication, plus an authentication exemption for the DCs
A tunnel rule between the payroll servers and the domain controllers
An inbound firewall rule that allows traffic only from the domain controllers' IP addresses
A server-to-server rule that requests authentication but doesn't require it

explanation: An isolation rule restricts connections to computers that authenticate with IPsec, and an authentication exemption rule lets computers such as domain controllers communicate without IPsec. Tunnel rules protect traffic between gateway endpoints, an ordinary firewall rule doesn't require IPsec authentication and requesting authentication without requiring it still accepts unauthenticated computers.

prompt: Members of the IT-Admins global security group must use passwords of at least 20 characters, while other users keep the 12-character domain policy. How should the administrator implement this?

options.text: Link a GPO with a 20-character minimum password length to the OU that contains IT-Admins
Create a password settings object with a 20-character minimum and apply it to IT-Admins
Edit the Default Domain Policy and filter it to the IT-Admins group
Create a password settings object and link it to the OU that contains the IT-Admins users

explanation: Fine-grained password policies are password settings objects (PSOs) that apply to users and global security groups and override the domain password policy for them. Password policy in an OU-linked GPO doesn't apply to domain accounts, the Default Domain Policy applies to the whole domain and PSOs can't be applied to OUs.

prompt: A user belongs to two groups that have password settings objects applied: PSO-A with precedence 10 and PSO-B with precedence 20. No PSO is applied directly to the user. Which policy applies to the user?

options.text: PSO-B, because the higher precedence value wins
The Default Domain Policy, because the PSOs conflict
Whichever PSO was created most recently
PSO-A, because the lowest precedence value wins

explanation: When several PSOs apply through group membership, the one with the lowest precedence number wins, and a PSO applied directly to a user would take priority over group-applied PSOs. Conflicting PSOs don't fall back to the domain policy, and creation date doesn't matter.

prompt: An administrator links a GPO that sets a 16-character minimum password length to the Finance OU, but Finance users can still set 12-character domain passwords. Why?

options.text: Domain account password policy comes only from domain-linked GPOs
The GPO must be enforced to override the Default Domain Policy
Password settings apply only after the users' computers restart twice
Finance users must be added to the Protected Users group

explanation: Account policies for domain user accounts come only from GPOs linked to the domain, normally the Default Domain Policy, so an OU-linked password policy affects only local accounts on computers in that OU. Enforcing the link or restarting doesn't change this, and Protected Users doesn't set password length; a PSO is the supported way to give Finance a different policy.

prompt: An administrator is deploying Microsoft Entra Password Protection for AD DS. Domain controllers must not have any internet access. Which design meets this requirement?

options.text: Install the DC agent on every DC and give each DC outbound access to Microsoft Entra ID
Install the proxy service on every DC so that it downloads policy directly
Install the proxy service on internet-connected member servers and the DC agent on DCs
Install Microsoft Entra Connect on a DC and enable password hash synchronization

explanation: The DC agent doesn't need internet access; it obtains the password policy through the proxy service, which runs on member servers that can reach Microsoft Entra ID, and the policy is stored in SYSVOL. Giving DCs outbound access, or running the proxy service on DCs so they download policy, breaks the requirement, and password hash synchronization doesn't enforce banned passwords.

prompt: Before enforcing Microsoft Entra Password Protection on-premises, the security team wants to see how many password changes would be rejected, without blocking anyone. What should be configured?

options.text: Set Enforce custom list to No
Set the on-premises mode to Audit
Remove the DC agent from half of the domain controllers
Disable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory

explanation: Audit mode logs password changes and resets that would have been rejected in the DC agent's event log without blocking them. Turning off the custom list still enforces the global banned password list, removing agents from some DCs makes enforcement inconsistent and disabling password protection stops evaluation, so nothing is logged.

prompt: After administrators were added to the Protected Users group, they can no longer sign in to a legacy management application, which reports an authentication error. Other users can sign in. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Protected Users members have a TGT lifetime of 10 hours
Protected Users members must use smart cards to sign in
Protected Users members can't sign in to domain controllers
The application uses NTLM, which Protected Users members can't use

explanation: Members of Protected Users can't authenticate with NTLM and must use Kerberos with AES, so applications that depend on NTLM fail for them. Their TGT lifetime is limited to four hours, smart cards aren't required and membership doesn't block sign-in to domain controllers.

prompt: An administrator plans to add every privileged account to Protected Users, including the service accounts that run SQL Server and the computer accounts of management servers. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Leave service and computer accounts out of Protected Users
Add all of them, because Protected Users is designed for service accounts
Add only the computer accounts, because they support AES
Add the service accounts only after raising the domain functional level to Windows Server 2025

explanation: Microsoft warns never to add service or computer accounts to Protected Users, because membership gives them no local protection and restrictions such as no NTLM and no delegation can break them. Protected Users is meant for user accounts, and raising the functional level doesn't change this guidance; the group's DC-side protections need the Windows Server 2012 R2 domain functional level.

prompt: An administrator is hardening a new Windows Server 2025 domain controller and wants to apply Microsoft's role-specific security baseline with drift control. Which command should be run?

options.text: Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/MemberServer -Default
Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecuredCore -Default
Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario SecurityBaseline/WindowsServer/2025/DomainController -Default
Set-OSConfigDesiredConfiguration -Scenario Defender/Antivirus/WindowsServer/2025 -Default

explanation: The DomainController scenario applies the Windows Server 2025 baseline tailored to domain controllers, and OSConfig then protects those settings from drift. The MemberServer scenario targets domain-joined member servers, while SecuredCore and the Defender Antivirus scenario are companion baselines that don't apply the DC role's settings.

prompt: Only members of Domain Admins should be able to sign in locally to domain controllers. Where should the administrator configure this?

options.text: In the Default Domain Policy, under Password Policy
In the Default Domain Controllers Policy, Allow log on locally
In a GPO linked to the Users container, under Restricted Groups
On the Log On To setting of each user account in Active Directory Users and Computers

explanation: User rights for domain controllers come from GPOs linked to the Domain Controllers OU, such as the Default Domain Controllers Policy, where Allow log on locally defines who can sign in at the console. Password policy doesn't control logon rights, GPOs can't be linked to the Users container and Log On To limits which computers each user can use rather than who can use the DCs.

prompt: Tier 0 administrator accounts must be able to sign in only to domain controllers and dedicated privileged access workstations, even if their credentials are stolen. What should the administrator implement?

options.text: Logon hours on each Tier 0 account
Universal group membership caching for the Tier 0 site
A fine-grained password policy for Tier 0 accounts
An authentication policy silo for the Tier 0 accounts

explanation: Authentication policies and authentication policy silos restrict the hosts from which an account can obtain Kerberos tickets, and they require the Windows Server 2012 R2 or later domain functional level. Logon hours limit when accounts can sign in, universal group membership caching speeds logons in sites without a global catalog and password policies don't restrict where accounts are used.

prompt: A Domain Admins account must never have its credentials delegated by any service, even one trusted for delegation, and the account can't be added to Protected Users. Which account option should be enabled?

options.text: Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated
Use only Kerberos DES encryption types for this account
Do not require Kerberos preauthentication
Store password using reversible encryption

explanation: Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated prevents services from delegating the account's credentials. DES encryption is insecure and disabled by default, removing the preauthentication requirement exposes the account to offline password attacks and reversible encryption stores the password in a recoverable form.

prompt: A security assessment reports that several user accounts are vulnerable to AS-REP roasting. Which account setting should the administrator look for and clear?

options.text: User must change password at next logon
Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated
Do not require Kerberos preauthentication
This account supports Kerberos AES 256 bit encryption

explanation: Accounts with Do not require Kerberos preauthentication let anyone request authentication data encrypted with the user's key and crack it offline, which is AS-REP roasting. Forcing a password change, preventing delegation and supporting AES don't create that exposure.

prompt: An auditor finds that a help desk group was added to Backup Operators so that it could run file server backups. Why is this a concern?

options.text: Members can create new domain user accounts
Members can sign in to DCs and back up the AD database
Members can modify Group Policy objects in SYSVOL
Members are added to Domain Admins by default

explanation: Backup Operators can sign in locally to domain controllers and back up files regardless of permissions, including the AD DS database and its secrets, so membership is effectively highly privileged. The group can't create users or edit GPOs by default, and its members aren't added to Domain Admins.

prompt: An administrator delegated permissions on a user account that is a member of Domain Admins, but within an hour the delegated permissions disappear. What is causing this?

options.text: The KCC rebuilds the account's ACL during replication
Group Policy refresh resets permissions on user objects every 90 minutes
The PDC emulator removes delegations made outside the Delegation of Control Wizard
The SDProp process resets the ACLs of protected accounts to match AdminSDHolder

explanation: Every 60 minutes by default, SDProp compares protected accounts and groups with the ACL on the AdminSDHolder object and overwrites differences. The KCC manages the replication topology, Group Policy refresh doesn't reset AD object permissions and nothing removes permissions based on whether the Delegation of Control Wizard was used.

prompt: Help desk staff must be able to reset passwords for users in the Sales OU only, without any other administrative rights. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Use the Delegation of Control Wizard on the Sales OU
Add the help desk group to the Account Operators group
Add the help desk group to Domain Admins only during their shifts
Grant the help desk group Full Control on the domain object in ADSI Edit

explanation: Running the Delegation of Control Wizard on the Sales OU can grant the help desk group the Reset user passwords and force password change at next logon task for users in that OU only. Account Operators and Domain Admins grant far broader rights across the domain, and Full Control on the domain object gives control over the whole domain.

prompt: Any authenticated user in the domain can currently join up to 10 computers to the domain. Security requires that only the Desktop-Admins group can join computers. Which two actions should the administrator take?

options.text: Remove Authenticated Users from the Account Operators group
Add Desktop-Admins to the Domain Admins group
Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota on the domain to 0
Delegate Create Computer objects on the target OUs to Desktop-Admins
Enable Domain controller: Refuse setting default machine account password

explanation: The ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota attribute, 10 by default, lets authenticated users join that many computers, so setting it to 0 removes that ability, and delegating Create Computer objects on the OUs lets Desktop-Admins keep joining computers. Authenticated Users isn't a member of Account Operators, Domain Admins grants excessive rights and the default machine account password policy doesn't control who can join computers.

prompt: Before restricting NTLM in the domain, an administrator must identify which servers and applications still use NTLM to authenticate against domain controllers. What should be configured first?

options.text: Network security: Restrict NTLM: NTLM authentication in this domain set to Deny all
The Restrict NTLM: Audit NTLM authentication in this domain policy on DCs
Membership in the Protected Users group for all users
Kerberos client support for claims, compound authentication and armoring

explanation: Auditing NTLM authentication in the domain on domain controllers logs NTLM requests to the NTLM operational log without blocking them, so dependencies can be found before restrictions are applied. Deny all blocks NTLM immediately, adding everyone to Protected Users would break NTLM-dependent applications and Kerberos armoring doesn't report NTLM use.

prompt: A company creates a new AD DS forest with Windows Server 2025 domain controllers. A legacy application that performs SASL binds over LDAP without signing can't connect. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: New Windows Server 2025 AD deployments require LDAP signing by default
Windows Server 2025 domain controllers no longer accept LDAP on port 389
LDAP channel binding requires the application to use smart cards
Windows Server 2025 removed support for SASL binds

explanation: New Active Directory deployments with Windows Server 2025 require LDAP signing (sealing) by default for LDAP communication after a SASL bind, so unsigned binds fail. Port 389 is still used, channel binding applies to LDAP over TLS rather than smart cards and SASL binds remain supported.

prompt: A file server becomes slow during the day, and the administrator suspects memory pressure. Which Performance Monitor counters best confirm this?

options.text: Processor\% Processor Time and System\Processor Queue Length
PhysicalDisk\Avg. Disk Queue Length and PhysicalDisk\% Idle Time
Memory\Available MBytes and Memory\Pages/sec
Network Interface\Bytes Total/sec and Network Interface\Output Queue Length

explanation: Consistently low Memory\Available MBytes combined with high Memory\Pages/sec shows that the system is short of RAM and paging heavily. The processor counters measure CPU load, the disk counters measure storage utilization and the network counters measure throughput and congestion.

prompt: Users report slow responses from a database server. The administrator wants to know whether the storage is slow to answer read requests. Which counter should be examined?

options.text: PhysicalDisk\Avg. Disk sec/Read
Memory\Committed Bytes
Processor\% Interrupt Time
Server\Sessions Errored Out

explanation: Avg. Disk sec/Read is the average time each read takes, so sustained high values point to storage latency. Committed Bytes measures virtual memory commitment, % Interrupt Time measures time spent servicing hardware interrupts and Sessions Errored Out counts SMB server session errors.

prompt: An administrator wants a server to run a cleanup script automatically whenever free space on drive E: drops below 10 percent. Which Performance Monitor feature should be used?

options.text: A data collector set based on the System Performance template
A performance counter data collector set saved as a binary log
A configuration data collector set that records registry keys
A performance counter alert with a task that runs the script

explanation: A performance counter alert data collector set watches a counter such as LogicalDisk\% Free Space against a threshold and can log an event or start a task when it's crossed. The System Performance template and counter logs only collect data, and configuration data collectors record registry and WMI state.

prompt: An administrator wants to create a performance counter data collector set on 20 Server Core installations by using a script. Which tool should be used?

options.text: wevtutil
logman
typeperf
relog

explanation: logman creates, starts, stops and manages data collector sets from the command line, including on remote computers. wevtutil manages event logs, typeperf displays counter values without creating a data collector set and relog converts or filters existing performance logs.

prompt: An administrator wants to view live performance counters for several remote servers side by side in a browser, without signing in to the servers through Remote Desktop. Which tool fits best?

options.text: Resource Monitor
Reliability Monitor
The Performance Monitor tool in Windows Admin Center
Task Manager opened on each server through an RDP session

explanation: Windows Admin Center includes a Performance Monitor tool that displays counters from managed servers in the browser and can save workspaces. Resource Monitor, Reliability Monitor and Task Manager run locally, so each server would require an interactive sign-in.

prompt: An administrator wants Windows Server to predict when a data volume will run out of space, based on its own historical usage, without sending data to the cloud. What should be used?

options.text: System Insights volume consumption forecasting
Azure Monitor VM insights with the Map feature enabled
Storage Spaces Direct health service faults
File Server Resource Manager storage reports for each volume

explanation: System Insights runs machine learning models locally on Windows Server, and its volume consumption forecasting capability predicts future usage for each volume. VM insights sends data to Azure and its Map feature shows dependencies, the S2D health service reports current faults and FSRM storage reports describe current usage rather than forecasts.

prompt: An administrator wants to run the CPU capacity forecasting capability of System Insights immediately instead of waiting for its schedule, and then view the prediction. Which cmdlets should be used?

options.text: Start-ScheduledTask, then Get-ScheduledTaskInfo
Get-Counter, then Export-Counter
Get-InsightsCapability, then Enable-InsightsCapability
Invoke-InsightsCapability, then Get-InsightsCapabilityResult

explanation: Invoke-InsightsCapability runs a capability on demand, and Get-InsightsCapabilityResult returns its latest prediction. Get-InsightsCapability lists capabilities and Enable-InsightsCapability turns one on without producing a result, while the scheduled task and counter cmdlets don't run System Insights predictions.

prompt: Several hundred servers must forward selected events to a central collector, and the administrator doesn't want to list each source computer in the subscription. What should be configured?

options.text: A collector-initiated subscription with every server added as a source
A source-initiated subscription, with sources pointed at it by Group Policy
A data collector set on each server that writes to a network share
A larger Forwarded Events log on each source server

explanation: In a source-initiated subscription, source computers learn which collector to use from the Configure target Subscription Manager policy, so new servers are included without editing the subscription. A collector-initiated subscription lists each source, data collector sets gather performance data rather than forwarding events and the Forwarded Events log on the sources isn't used for forwarding.

prompt: The Security log on a domain controller fills quickly and overwrites events that auditors need. Events must be kept, and the server must keep logging. Which event log setting should be configured?

options.text: Overwrite events as needed (oldest events first)
Do not overwrite events (Clear logs manually)
Archive the log when full, do not overwrite events
Set the maximum log size to 1 MB

explanation: Archive the log when full saves the full log to a file and starts a new one, so no events are lost and logging continues. Overwriting discards old events, Do not overwrite events stops new events from being recorded once the log is full and a smaller log makes the problem worse.

prompt: An administrator regularly needs to see all Critical and Error events from the System, Application and Directory Service logs together in Event Viewer. What should be created?

options.text: A custom view that filters those logs by level
An event subscription on the same server
A data collector set with an event trace provider
An attached task for each event ID

explanation: A custom view saves a filter across several logs and event levels so the matching events appear together. A subscription forwards events between computers, an event trace data collector records ETW traces and attached tasks run actions for specific events rather than presenting them.

prompt: An administrator is creating a data collection rule for the Azure Monitor Agent and wants to collect only event ID 7036 from the System log to reduce ingestion costs. What should be configured in the rule?

options.text: A performance counter with a 60-second sample rate
A workspace transformation that drops all System log events
The basic Windows event log option with the System log selected
A custom XPath query such as System!*[System[(EventID=7036)]]

explanation: Data collection rules accept XPath queries that collect only matching events, which reduces the data sent to the workspace. Performance counters collect metrics, dropping all System events would also drop 7036 and the basic option collects whole logs by severity level.

prompt: Arc-enabled on-premises servers must send performance counters and Windows event logs to a Log Analytics workspace according to a data collection rule. What must be installed on the servers?

options.text: The Log Analytics agent (Microsoft Monitoring Agent)
The Azure Monitor Agent extension
The Dependency agent on its own
The Windows Admin Center extension

explanation: Data collection rules are used by the Azure Monitor Agent, which is deployed to Arc-enabled servers as a VM extension and associated with the rule. The Log Analytics agent is retired and doesn't use DCRs, the Dependency agent supports the VM insights Map feature alongside the Azure Monitor Agent and the Windows Admin Center extension provides management rather than data collection.

prompt: An administrator wants an alert when event ID 4625 (failed sign-in) appears more than 50 times in 10 minutes in data collected from servers into a Log Analytics workspace. Which type of alert rule should be created?

options.text: A log search alert rule with a KQL query
An activity log alert rule on the servers' resources
A metric alert rule on the Percentage CPU metric
A service health alert for the region

explanation: Log search alert rules run a query on a schedule and fire when the results cross a threshold, which suits counting events in a workspace. Activity log alerts react to Azure control plane operations, metric alerts evaluate metrics and service health alerts report Azure service issues.

prompt: Several alert rules must notify the on-call team by SMS and email and also start an Azure Automation runbook. What should the administrator configure once and reuse across the rules?

options.text: An alert processing rule that suppresses notifications
A data collection endpoint
An action group
A Log Analytics workspace transformation

explanation: An action group defines notifications such as SMS and email and actions such as starting a runbook, and many alert rules can use it. Alert processing rules can suppress notifications or add action groups during periods such as maintenance, data collection endpoints receive monitoring data and transformations modify ingested data.

prompt: An administrator enabled VM insights on Azure VMs and sees performance charts, but the Map view that shows processes and connections between servers is empty. What should be added?

options.text: Boot diagnostics on each VM
An Azure Network Watcher connection monitor for the VMs
The Custom Script Extension
The Dependency agent alongside the Azure Monitor Agent

explanation: The VM insights Map feature relies on the Dependency agent to discover processes and network connections, in addition to the Azure Monitor Agent that collects performance data. Boot diagnostics captures console screenshots and serial logs, Connection monitor tests connectivity between endpoints and the Custom Script Extension runs scripts.

prompt: Users can't open shares on file server FS3. From a client, an administrator wants to check whether TCP port 445 on FS3 is reachable. Which command should be used?

options.text: Resolve-DnsName FS3 -Type SRV
Test-NetConnection FS3 -Port 445
Get-NetIPConfiguration -Detailed
ping FS3 -t

explanation: Test-NetConnection with -Port attempts a TCP connection and reports whether it succeeded, along with name resolution and ping results. Resolve-DnsName only resolves names, Get-NetIPConfiguration shows local settings and ping tests ICMP, which doesn't show whether port 445 is open.

prompt: An Azure VM doesn't accept RDP connections from the admin network, and the administrator needs to know which network security group rule is blocking the traffic. Which tool provides this directly?

options.text: Azure Bastion
Boot diagnostics
VM insights Map
Network Watcher IP flow verify

explanation: IP flow verify tests whether a packet with a given source, destination, port and protocol is allowed or denied for a VM and names the NSG rule responsible. Bastion offers another connection path, boot diagnostics shows console output and the VM insights Map shows observed connections rather than the rule that denies traffic.

prompt: A web server's DNS record was changed to a new IP address, and the DNS server returns the new address. A client still connects to the old address. What should the administrator do on the client first?

options.text: Run Clear-DnsClientCache
Run Register-DnsClient
Restart the Netlogon service
Run Set-DnsClientServerAddress -ResetServerAddresses

explanation: The client is using a cached answer, so Clear-DnsClientCache (or ipconfig /flushdns) removes it and forces a new query. Register-DnsClient registers the client's own records, Netlogon registers DC records and resetting the DNS server list changes which servers are queried without clearing the cache.

prompt: One server resolves intranet.contoso.com to an old IP address even after its DNS cache is cleared, while other computers resolve the correct address. On that server, Resolve-DnsName -DnsOnly returns the correct address. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The record's TTL in the DNS zone has expired
The server uses a different DNS suffix search list
A stale entry for the name in the server's hosts file
A conditional forwarder configured on the DNS server

explanation: Resolve-DnsName -DnsOnly bypasses the hosts file and returns the right answer, so a stale hosts file entry is overriding DNS, and hosts entries are reloaded into the cache after it's cleared. TTL and forwarder issues would affect the DNS query itself, and a fully qualified name isn't affected by the suffix search list.

prompt: An administrator needs a readable Windows Update log from a Windows Server 2025 server to investigate failed update installations. What should the administrator run?

options.text: wevtutil qe System /f:text
Get-WindowsUpdateLog
Get-HotFix
sfc /scannow

explanation: Windows Update writes ETW traces, and Get-WindowsUpdateLog merges them into a readable WindowsUpdate.log file. wevtutil queries event logs, Get-HotFix lists installed updates and sfc checks protected system files.

prompt: Cumulative updates repeatedly fail to install on a server with errors that point to component store corruption. What should the administrator run first?

options.text: chkdsk C: /f
wuauclt /detectnow
Reset-ComputerMachinePassword
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth

explanation: DISM /RestoreHealth scans and repairs the component store that servicing uses, after which sfc /scannow can repair system files. chkdsk checks the file system, wuauclt /detectnow is a legacy detection trigger that fixes nothing and resetting the machine password affects the domain secure channel.

prompt: The PDC emulator of the forest root domain must take its time from the external NTP source pool.ntp.org, while the rest of the forest follows the domain hierarchy. Which command should be run on the PDC emulator?

options.text: w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:pool.ntp.org /syncfromflags:manual /reliable:yes /update
w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:pool.ntp.org /syncfromflags:domhier /update
w32tm /resync /rediscover
w32tm /query /source

explanation: On the forest root PDC emulator, /manualpeerlist with /syncfromflags:manual sets the external source, /reliable:yes advertises it as a reliable time source and /update applies the change, while other DCs and members keep following the hierarchy. With domhier the manual peer list isn't used, /resync forces a sync with the current source and /query /source only displays it.

prompt: The Processor\% Processor Time counter in a Hyper-V host's management OS stays low, yet VMs on the host are slow and appear CPU-starved. Which counter shows the actual physical CPU usage of the host?

options.text: System\Processor Queue Length in the management OS
Processor\% Privileged Time in the management OS
Hyper-V Hypervisor Logical Processor\% Total Run Time
Hyper-V Dynamic Memory Balancer\Average Pressure

explanation: On a Hyper-V host the management OS is itself a partition, so its Processor counters don't include VM workloads, whereas Hyper-V Hypervisor Logical Processor\% Total Run Time shows how busy the physical processors are. The queue length and privileged time counters also describe only the management OS, and Average Pressure reflects memory demand.

prompt: The Custom Script Extension fails on an Azure Windows VM, and the portal shows only a generic error. Where on the VM should the administrator look for the extension's detailed logs?

options.text: C:\ProgramData\GuestConfig\ext_mgr_logs
C:\WindowsAzure\Logs\Plugins
C:\Windows\Logs\CBS
C:\Windows\Panther

explanation: On Azure VMs, the Azure VM Agent writes extension logs under C:\WindowsAzure\Logs\Plugins, in a folder for each extension. C:\ProgramData\GuestConfig\ext_mgr_logs is used by the Azure Arc Connected Machine agent, the CBS folder holds servicing logs and Panther holds Windows Setup logs.

prompt: An extension stays in a Creating state on an Azure Arc-enabled Windows Server. The administrator first wants to confirm that the agent is connected and its dependent services are running. Which command should be used?

options.text: azcmagent check
azcmagent logs
azcmagent disconnect
azcmagent show

explanation: azcmagent show reports the agent's connection status and the state of its dependent services, which must be running for extensions to deploy. azcmagent check tests network connectivity to the required endpoints, azcmagent logs collects logs for support and azcmagent disconnect removes the machine's connection to Azure.

prompt: On an Arc-enabled server, the agent and its services are healthy, but an extension is in a Failed state. The log in C:\ProgramData\GuestConfig\ext_mgr_logs shows a download error that has since been fixed. What should the administrator do next?

options.text: Remove the extension and install it again
Run azcmagent disconnect and then connect the server again
Delete the C:\ProgramData\GuestConfig folder and restart the server
Restart the Windows Update service

explanation: Microsoft recommends removing an extension that isn't in a Succeeded state, for example with Remove-AzConnectedMachineExtension, and then installing it again. Disconnecting deletes the machine's Azure resource, deleting the GuestConfig folder removes agent data and the Windows Update service isn't involved in Arc extension installation.

prompt: After a BIOS firmware update, a BitLocker-protected server starts at the BitLocker recovery screen. How should the administrator avoid this during future firmware updates?

options.text: Remove the TPM protector permanently and use a password protector
Turn off BitLocker with manage-bde -off before each update
Run Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RebootCount 1 before the update
Clear the TPM in the firmware after each update

explanation: Suspending BitLocker before a firmware update skips TPM validation for the specified number of restarts, and protection resumes automatically afterward. A password-only protector removes TPM protection, fully decrypting the drive takes a long time and leaves it unprotected and clearing the TPM forces recovery.

prompt: A server shows the BitLocker recovery screen, and its recovery password was backed up to AD DS. How can a domain administrator find the password in Active Directory Users and Computers?

options.text: Open the account of the last user who signed in and check its Security tab
Install the BitLocker Recovery Password Viewer and check the computer object
Run Get-LapsADPassword for the computer
Read the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd attribute in the computer object's Attribute Editor tab

explanation: The BitLocker Recovery Password Viewer feature adds a BitLocker Recovery tab to computer objects, which displays the msFVE-RecoveryInformation child objects stored under the computer. User objects don't hold the key, Get-LapsADPassword returns local administrator passwords and ms-Mcs-AdmPwd is the legacy LAPS password attribute.

prompt: A physical disk in a Storage Spaces pool failed and has been replaced with a new disk that was added to the pool. The virtual disk still shows a degraded state. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Run Optimize-Volume -ReTrim on the volume that the virtual disk hosts
Run Initialize-Disk against the virtual disk
Run chkdsk /r on the virtual disk's volume
Retire and remove the failed disk, then run Repair-VirtualDisk

explanation: Retiring and removing the failed disk lets Storage Spaces rebuild data onto the remaining capacity, and Repair-VirtualDisk starts the repair, whose progress Get-StorageJob shows. Retrim and chkdsk act on the file system rather than the virtual disk's resiliency, and initializing the disk would destroy its partitions.

prompt: Event logs report NTFS corruption on a large data volume of a file server that must stay online during business hours. What should the administrator run first?

options.text: chkdsk E: /scan
chkdsk E: /f /r
format E: /fs:refs
Repair-VirtualDisk

explanation: chkdsk /scan runs an online scan of an NTFS volume and queues any fixes, so a later spot-fix pass takes the volume offline only briefly. chkdsk /f /r locks the volume for a long time, formatting destroys the data and Repair-VirtualDisk repairs Storage Spaces resiliency rather than file system corruption.

prompt: An administrator wants to enable the Active Directory Recycle Bin in the contoso.com forest. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It can be enabled at any forest functional level and disabled later
It's enabled separately for each domain with Set-ADDomain
It needs the 2008 R2 forest functional level or higher and can't be turned off
It's enabled automatically when the first Windows Server 2025 DC is promoted

explanation: The AD Recycle Bin requires the Windows Server 2008 R2 or later forest functional level and is enabled for the whole forest, for example with Enable-ADOptionalFeature 'Recycle Bin Feature' -Scope ForestOrConfigurationSet; it can't be disabled afterward. It isn't enabled per domain or automatically when a DC is promoted.

prompt: With the AD Recycle Bin enabled, the user account jsmith was deleted yesterday. Which approach restores it with its attributes and group memberships?

options.text: Restore-ADObject on the object found with Get-ADObject -IncludeDeletedObjects
Run New-ADUser -Name jsmith with the -Instance parameter set to the old account
Run an ntdsutil authoritative restore of the jsmith object from a backup
Enable-ADAccount -Identity jsmith

explanation: Get-ADObject with -IncludeDeletedObjects finds the object in the Deleted Objects container, and Restore-ADObject restores it with its attributes and link values such as group memberships. New-ADUser creates a new account with a new SID, an authoritative restore requires a backup and DSRM and Enable-ADAccount works only on an existing disabled account.

prompt: An OU named Sales was deleted along with its child OUs and users, and the AD Recycle Bin is enabled. In which order should the objects be restored?

options.text: The users first, then the child OUs, then the Sales OU
All objects at once, in any order
Only the Sales OU, because its children are restored with it
The Sales OU first, then the child OUs, then the users

explanation: A deleted object can be restored only into a parent that exists, so the hierarchy is restored from the top down: the Sales OU, then its child OUs, then the users. Restoring users first fails while their parent containers are still deleted, and restoring the parent OU doesn't automatically restore its children.

prompt: Before the AD Recycle Bin was enabled, an administrator accidentally deleted an OU containing 200 users. The administrator restores last night's system state backup on a DC in Directory Services Restore Mode. What must be done before restarting the DC normally?

options.text: Nothing, because a nonauthoritative restore replicates the OU to the other DCs
Run ntdsutil authoritative restore with restore subtree for the OU
Run repadmin /syncall /AdeP while the DC is still in DSRM
Enable the AD Recycle Bin and restore the OU with Restore-ADObject

explanation: After a nonauthoritative restore, inbound replication would delete the OU again, so it's marked authoritative with ntdsutil's authoritative restore and restore subtree commands, which raise version numbers so the OU replicates out. Replication doesn't run while the DC is in DSRM, and enabling the Recycle Bin now doesn't recover objects deleted before it was enabled.

prompt: An administrator needs to restore system state on a domain controller, but nobody knows its Directory Services Restore Mode password. The DC is still running normally. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reset the domain Administrator password, which also changes the DSRM password
Run Get-LapsADPassword, because DSRM passwords are always backed up by default
Run ntdsutil set dsrm password, then reset password on server null
Demote and repromote the DC to set a new DSRM password

explanation: ntdsutil's set dsrm password command resets the DSRM administrator password on a running DC, and reset password on server null targets the local server. The domain Administrator account is separate from the DSRM account, Windows LAPS manages the DSRM password only if configured to and demoting and repromoting is needlessly disruptive.

prompt: SYSVOL content was corrupted on every domain controller, and a good copy was restored from backup on DC1. The domain uses DFS Replication for SYSVOL. How should DC1's SYSVOL be made authoritative?

options.text: Set msDFSR-Options=1 on DC1, disable SYSVOL replication on all DCs, then enable DC1 first
Run dfsrmig /setglobalstate 3 on DC1 to restart SYSVOL migration from FRS
Copy the restored SYSVOL folder from DC1 to every other DC with Robocopy
Run ntdsutil authoritative restore on DC1 and restore the subtree that holds SYSVOL

explanation: An authoritative SYSVOL restore with DFS Replication sets msDFSR-Options to 1 on DC1's SYSVOL subscription, sets msDFSR-Enabled to FALSE on every DC and then enables DC1 first so the others sync from it. dfsrmig controls FRS-to-DFSR migration, copying files with Robocopy bypasses DFSR and causes conflicts and ntdsutil authoritative restore applies to AD objects rather than SYSVOL files.

prompt: One domain controller's SYSVOL is out of date and has stopped replicating, while the other DCs are healthy. The administrator wants this DC to discard its copy and resync from a partner. What should be done?

options.text: Set msDFSR-Options to 1 on that DC's SYSVOL subscription
Run repadmin /syncall /AdeP on that DC and restart the DFSR service
Delete the SYSVOL folder on that DC and restart the Netlogon service
Toggle msDFSR-Enabled off and on for that DC, with dfsrdiag pollad

explanation: A nonauthoritative SYSVOL sync sets msDFSR-Enabled to FALSE for that DC, waits for AD replication and runs dfsrdiag pollad, then sets it back to TRUE so DFSR performs an initial sync from a partner. msDFSR-Options=1 would make this DC authoritative and overwrite the good copies, repadmin replicates AD rather than SYSVOL files and deleting SYSVOL manually breaks the share.

prompt: A domain controller that was offline for eight months is reconnected. Replication from it fails, and event ID 2042 reports that it has been too long since the machine replicated. The tombstone lifetime is 180 days. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Increase the tombstone lifetime and force replication with repadmin /syncall
Forcibly remove the DC, clean up its metadata and promote it again
Run Restore-ADObject on the DC's computer account
Disable strict replication consistency and restart the DC

explanation: A DC that hasn't replicated for longer than the tombstone lifetime can reintroduce deleted objects as lingering objects, so the safe fix is to forcibly remove it, clean up its metadata and rebuild it. Raising the tombstone lifetime afterward risks reintroducing deleted objects, Restore-ADObject restores deleted objects and disabling strict replication consistency would let lingering objects replicate.

prompt: repadmin /showrepl on DC2 shows replication from DC5 failing with error 1722, The RPC server is unavailable. What should the administrator check first?

options.text: The tombstone lifetime configured for the forest
Whether the AD Recycle Bin is enabled in the forest
DC5's name resolution and RPC firewall access
The forest and domain functional levels of the DCs

explanation: Error 1722 means DC2 couldn't establish an RPC connection to DC5, typically because of DNS problems, a firewall blocking RPC (TCP 135 and the dynamic port range) or DC5 being offline. The tombstone lifetime, the Recycle Bin and the functional level don't cause RPC connectivity errors.

prompt: Clients can't locate a new domain controller, and its _ldap._tcp SRV record is missing from DNS although dynamic updates are allowed on the zone. What should the administrator do on the DC?

options.text: Restart the Netlogon service or run nltest /dsregdns
Run ipconfig /registerdns
Restart the DNS Client service
Run repadmin /kcc to rebuild the replication topology

explanation: The Netlogon service registers a DC's locator records from its netlogon.dns file, so restarting it or running nltest /dsregdns re-registers them. ipconfig /registerdns and the DNS Client service handle the computer's own A and PTR records, and repadmin /kcc recalculates the replication topology.

prompt: Users signing in to one member server get Kerberos authentication failures, and the System log shows KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reset the server's computer account password
Purge the users' Kerberos tickets with klist purge
Register a new SPN for the server's service account with setspn
Correct the server's clock so it's within five minutes of the DCs

explanation: KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW means the clock difference exceeds the Kerberos tolerance, five minutes by default, so the server's time synchronization with the domain hierarchy must be fixed, for example with w32tm. Resetting the machine password, purging tickets and registering SPNs don't correct clock skew.

prompt: After a service account change, Kerberos authentication to a web application fails and falls back to NTLM. The administrator suspects the same SPN is registered on two accounts. Which command finds duplicate SPNs across the forest?

options.text: setspn -L webapp
setspn -X -F
klist get HTTP/webapp.contoso.com
nltest /dsgetdc:contoso.com

explanation: setspn -X searches for duplicate SPNs, and -F extends the search to the whole forest. setspn -L lists the SPNs on one account, klist get requests a ticket for an SPN without detecting duplicates and nltest /dsgetdc locates a domain controller.

prompt: A user was added to a security group that grants access to a share on a file server. Without signing out, the user still gets access denied when opening the share. What can the user do to pick up the new membership?

options.text: Run klist purge and reconnect
Run gpupdate /force and reopen the share
Run ipconfig /flushdns
Run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair

explanation: Group memberships are carried in Kerberos tickets, so purging tickets with klist purge makes the client request new tickets that include the new group when it reconnects; signing out and in again also works. gpupdate refreshes policy, flushing DNS clears name resolution and Test-ComputerSecureChannel checks the computer's trust with the domain.

prompt: Users can't sign in to a member server with domain accounts, and the server reports that the trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed. The administrator can still sign in with a local administrator account. What is the least disruptive fix?

options.text: Remove the server from the domain and join it again
Reset the computer account in Active Directory Users and Computers and restart the server
Run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair with domain credentials
Restore the server from yesterday's backup

explanation: Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair resets the computer's password locally and in AD DS without a rejoin or restart. Leaving and rejoining the domain or restoring a backup is more disruptive, and resetting the account in Active Directory Users and Computers alone leaves the secure channel broken until the computer rejoins.

prompt: From a member server, an administrator wants to check whether its secure channel with the contoso.com domain is healthy and which domain controller it uses. Which command should be run?

options.text: repadmin /showrepl
dcdiag /test:netlogons
w32tm /monitor
nltest /sc_verify:contoso.com

explanation: nltest /sc_verify verifies the secure channel with the domain and reports the DC it's established with. repadmin /showrepl and dcdiag report on domain controller replication and health rather than a member server's secure channel, and w32tm /monitor shows time offsets.
